records.title: Present Simple: habits and routines
records.objective: Describe repeated everyday actions and routines.

concept.en: Use the Present Simple for repeated actions, habits and routines.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại đơn để nói về hành động lặp lại, thói quen và lịch sinh hoạt thường xuyên.

formulae: Subject + base verb (+ s/es with he/she/it).
whenToUse: Regular routines and habits.
Repeated actions with frequency expressions such as every day, usually and often.

positive: I work at home on Fridays.
She takes the bus every morning.
question: Do you exercise every day?
Does she start at nine?

variations: Frequency adverbs usually come before the main verb but after be.

records.title: Present Continuous: actions happening now
records.objective: Describe actions in progress at the speaking moment.

concept.en: Use the Present Continuous for an action in progress at the moment of speaking.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại tiếp diễn cho hành động đang diễn ra ngay tại thời điểm nói.

whenToUse: Something happening now.
A visible or immediate activity around the speaking moment.

positive: I am waiting now.
question: Are they coming now?

variations: Now, right now and at the moment often make the time reference explicit.

records.title: Present Perfect: life experience
records.objective: Talk about experience without stating a finished past time.

concept.en: Use the Present Perfect to talk about life experience when the exact finished time is not stated.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại hoàn thành để nói về trải nghiệm trong đời khi không nêu một thời điểm quá khứ đã kết thúc.

whenToUse: Ask whether an experience has happened at any time up to now.
State experience without a finished past-time expression.

positive: I have visited Singapore twice.
negative: She has never missed a flight.
question: Have you ever worked abroad?

variations: Use Past Simple if you add a finished time such as last year.

records.title: First Conditional
records.objective: Describe realistic future conditions and likely results.

concept.en: Use the First Conditional for a realistic future condition and its likely result.
concept.vi: Dùng Câu điều kiện loại 1 cho điều kiện có khả năng xảy ra trong tương lai và kết quả có thể xảy ra theo.

formulae: If + Present Simple, will + base verb.
will + base verb + if + Present Simple.
whenToUse: Realistic future plans and consequences.
Warnings, promises and practical decisions based on a future condition.

positive: If it rains, we will take a taxi.
negative: If the shop isn't open, we won't wait.
question: What will you do if the train is late?

variations: Result clauses can later use can, may, might or an imperative.

records.title: Present Perfect Simple vs Continuous
records.objective: Choose result/completion/count vs duration/activity focus.

concept.en: Choose Present Perfect Simple for completion/result/count and Present Perfect Continuous for duration or ongoing activity.
concept.vi: Chọn Hiện tại hoàn thành đơn khi nhấn mạnh kết quả, sự hoàn tất hoặc số lượng; chọn Hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn khi nhấn mạnh quá trình hoặc khoảng thời gian.

whenToUse: Contrast a completed result with an activity in progress or recently continuing.
Contrast how much/how many with how long.

positive: I have written three emails.
I have been writing emails for two hours.

variations: State verbs normally prefer the simple form.

records.title: Second Conditional
records.objective: Describe unlikely or hypothetical present/future situations.

concept.en: Use the Second Conditional for unlikely, imaginary or hypothetical present/future situations.
concept.vi: Dùng Câu điều kiện loại 2 cho tình huống hiện tại hoặc tương lai mang tính giả định, tưởng tượng hoặc khó xảy ra.

formulae: If + Past Simple, would + base verb.
would + base verb + if + Past Simple.
whenToUse: Imagine a different present or future.
Give hypothetical advice or discuss unlikely possibilities.

positive: If I had more time, I would learn another language.
negative: If we didn't need the car, we would sell it.
question: What would you do if your flight were cancelled?

variations: Were is common for hypothetical be, especially in careful/formal English.

records.title: Third Conditional
records.objective: Describe unreal past conditions and imagined past results.

concept.en: Use the Third Conditional to imagine a different past condition and a different past result.
concept.vi: Dùng Câu điều kiện loại 3 để tưởng tượng một điều kiện trong quá khứ đã không xảy ra và kết quả quá khứ khác đi.

formulae: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle.
whenToUse: Past regrets and hindsight.
Alternative outcomes for completed past events.

positive: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train.
negative: If I hadn't missed the call, I wouldn't have been late.
question: What would you have done if the booking had failed?

variations: Could have and might have can replace would have to change result meaning.

records.title: Reporting passives
records.objective: Use It is said that... and subject + is believed to... patterns.

concept.en: Use reporting passives to present reported information while distancing the writer from the source.
concept.vi: Dùng cấu trúc bị động tường thuật để trình bày thông tin được cho là đúng và tạo khoảng cách giữa người viết với nguồn thông tin.

formulae: Subject + be + past participle + to have + past participle.
whenToUse: News, reports and formal summaries where the source is general or secondary.
Claims where the writer does not want to present the proposition as a direct personal assertion.

positive: The policy is expected to reduce delays.
The company is reported to have opened a new office.

variations: Common reporting verbs include say, believe, expect, think, know and report.

records.title: Inversion after negative and restrictive adverbials
records.objective: Use Never/Rarely/Only then/Not until + auxiliary inversion for marked emphasis.

concept.en: After certain negative or restrictive expressions placed first, invert the auxiliary and subject for marked emphasis.
concept.vi: Khi đưa một số trạng từ/cụm từ phủ định hoặc hạn định lên đầu câu để nhấn mạnh, đảo trợ động từ lên trước chủ ngữ.

formulae: Negative/restrictive expression + auxiliary + subject + main verb.
Not until + clause + auxiliary + subject + main verb.
whenToUse: Formal writing, speeches and deliberate rhetorical emphasis.
Emphasize rarity, restriction or a delayed realization.

positive: Rarely do we see such a clear improvement.
Only then did the team understand the risk.

variations: Common triggers include never, rarely, seldom, hardly, not until and only then.

records.title: Nominalisation in formal writing
records.objective: Convert processes/qualities into noun phrases without producing dense unnatural prose.

concept.en: Nominalisation turns actions or qualities into noun phrases, often creating denser formal writing.
concept.vi: Danh từ hóa biến hành động hoặc đặc tính thành cụm danh từ, thường giúp văn phong trang trọng và cô đọng hơn nhưng có thể làm câu nặng nếu lạm dụng.

formulae: evaluate → evaluation; expand → expansion; decide → decision
whenToUse: Formal reports and academic writing where processes are discussed as concepts.
Package information into a noun phrase for cohesion or comparison.

positive: The rapid expansion of the service created new staffing needs.

variations: Prefer a finite verb when nominalisation would hide the actor or make the sentence unnecessarily dense.

records.title: Epistemic vs deontic modal readings
records.objective: Disambiguate probability, obligation, permission and volition from context.

concept.en: Interpret modal verbs by context because the same modal can express probability, obligation, permission or volition.
concept.vi: Giải thích động từ khuyết thiếu dựa vào ngữ cảnh vì cùng một modal có thể biểu thị suy đoán, nghĩa vụ, sự cho phép hoặc ý chí.

whenToUse: Resolve meaning when a modal form has more than one possible semantic reading.
Choose surrounding context that makes epistemic and deontic meanings clear.

positive: They must be asleep. (deduction)
Visitors must wear a badge. (obligation)
You may use this room. (permission)

variations: Prosody, subject choice, lexical aspect and surrounding discourse can remove or create ambiguity.

records.title: Marked word order for rhetorical effect
records.objective: Use fronting, inversion and end-focus intentionally rather than accidentally.

concept.en: Marked word order moves information away from the neutral pattern to create focus, scene-setting or rhetorical rhythm.
concept.vi: Trật tự từ đánh dấu cố ý thay đổi trật tự trung tính để tạo điểm nhấn, dựng bối cảnh hoặc tạo nhịp điệu tu từ.

formulae: Fronted locative + verb + subject (with suitable verbs).
Fronted complement + linking verb + subject in selected formal styles.
whenToUse: Literary/descriptive scene-setting.
Formal rhetoric where the marked order improves information flow rather than merely sounding unusual.

positive: At the end of the corridor stood a narrow wooden door.
Most striking was the speed of the recovery.

variations: Marked order is register-sensitive and should not replace neutral SVO without a discourse reason.

records.title: Be: identification and description
records.objective: Use am/is/are to identify people/things and give simple descriptions.

concept.en: Use am, is and are to identify people or things and to give simple descriptions.
concept.vi: Dùng am, is và are để xác định người/vật hoặc đưa ra mô tả đơn giản.

whenToUse: Say who or what someone/something is.
Give a simple description, condition or location with be.

positive: I am a student in this class.
Leo is tall and friendly.
We are ready for the lesson.

variations: Use contracted forms I'm, he's, she's, it's, we're, you're and they're in common speech and informal writing.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Be: negatives
records.objective: Make negative statements with am not/isn't/aren't.

concept.en: Put not after am, is or are to make a negative statement with be.
concept.vi: Đặt not sau am, is hoặc are để tạo câu phủ định với động từ be.

whenToUse: Say that an identity, description, state or location is not true.

negative: I am not tired this morning.
The small shop isn't open yet.

variations: Amn't is not standard in most varieties of English; use am not.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Be: yes/no questions and short answers
records.objective: Ask and answer basic yes/no questions with be.

concept.en: Move am, is or are before the subject to make a yes/no question, and answer with the matching form of be.
concept.vi: Đưa am, is hoặc are lên trước chủ ngữ để tạo câu hỏi yes/no và trả lời ngắn bằng đúng dạng của be.

whenToUse: Check identity, description, state or location.
Give a short yes/no answer without repeating the whole sentence.

question: Are you ready for the lesson?
Is Maya at home this evening?
Are they students in this class?

variations: In negative short answers, isn't and aren't are common: No, he isn't. No, they aren't.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Subject pronouns
records.objective: Choose I/you/he/she/it/we/they correctly as subjects.

concept.en: Use subject pronouns before the verb to show who or what performs the action or has the state.
concept.vi: Dùng đại từ chủ ngữ trước động từ để chỉ người/vật thực hiện hành động hoặc mang trạng thái.

formulae: I / you / he / she / it / we / they + verb or be form.
whenToUse: Avoid repeating a known person's or thing's name.
Choose a pronoun that matches person and number.

positive: She is my sister Anna.
They live near this station.
It is very small but useful.

variations: Use it for one thing, animal or situation when gender is not relevant; use they for plural people or things.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Possessive adjectives
records.objective: Use my/your/his/her/its/our/their before nouns.

concept.en: Use a possessive adjective before a noun to show who the noun belongs or relates to.
concept.vi: Dùng tính từ sở hữu trước danh từ để chỉ danh từ đó thuộc về hoặc có liên hệ với ai.

whenToUse: Show ownership or a close relationship before a noun.

positive: My phone is new this week.
His name is Daniel Park.
Our classroom is upstairs on the left.

variations: Possessive adjectives do not take an article before them: my bag, not the my bag.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: This/that/these/those
records.objective: Choose demonstratives for singular/plural and near/far reference.

concept.en: Use this/these for things that feel near and that/those for things that feel farther away; match singular and plural.
concept.vi: Dùng this/these cho vật ở gần và that/those cho vật ở xa hơn; đồng thời chọn đúng dạng số ít hoặc số nhiều.

whenToUse: Point to or identify people and things by distance and number.

positive: This book is useful for beginners.
That bus is full this morning.
These apples are fresh today.

variations: This and that are singular; these and those are plural.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: There is / there are
records.objective: Introduce the existence and location of people and things.

concept.en: Use there is for one thing and there are for more than one thing when introducing what exists in a place or situation.
concept.vi: Dùng there is với một vật và there are với nhiều vật để giới thiệu sự tồn tại của người/vật trong một nơi hoặc tình huống.

whenToUse: Say that something exists or is present.
Introduce things in a place before giving more detail.

positive: There is a bank near this station.
There are two large windows in this classroom.
negative: There isn't a bus stop on this street.
question: Is there a pharmacy near this station?
Are there any free seats in this room?

variations: Use there's as a common contraction of there is.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: A/an for classification and first mention
records.objective: Use a/an with singular count nouns for non-specific reference.

concept.en: Use a or an before one non-specific singular count noun; choose an before a vowel sound and a before a consonant sound.
concept.vi: Dùng a hoặc an trước một danh từ đếm được số ít chưa xác định; dùng an trước âm nguyên âm và a trước âm phụ âm.

formulae: a + singular count noun beginning with a consonant sound
an + singular count noun beginning with a vowel sound
whenToUse: Classify a person or thing.
Mention one non-specific singular count noun for the first time.

positive: She is a doctor at this clinic.
I have an umbrella in my bag.
We have a small apartment near the station.

variations: Choose a/an by sound, not simply by the first written letter.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: The for basic specific reference
records.objective: Use the when speaker and listener can identify the referent.

concept.en: Use the before a noun when the speaker and listener can identify the specific person or thing.
concept.vi: Dùng the trước danh từ khi cả người nói và người nghe đều xác định được người hoặc vật cụ thể đang được nhắc tới.

formulae: the + uncountable noun when the reference is specific
whenToUse: Refer to something already mentioned.
Refer to a person or thing that is clear from the situation.

positive: I saw a dog. The dog was very friendly.
Please close the window near the door.
The water in this bottle is cold.

variations: Do not use the just because a noun is singular; use it when the reference is specific and identifiable.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Singular and plural nouns
records.objective: Form regular plurals and high-frequency irregular plurals.

concept.en: Use a singular noun for one countable item and a plural noun for more than one; many plurals take -s or -es, while some common nouns are irregular.
concept.vi: Dùng danh từ số ít cho một vật đếm được và danh từ số nhiều cho nhiều hơn một; nhiều danh từ thêm -s hoặc -es, còn một số danh từ thông dụng có dạng bất quy tắc.

whenToUse: Match the noun form to the number of countable people or things.
Use common irregular plurals such as children, men and women when needed.

positive: There is one book on the desk.
There are three buses outside.
Two children are playing in the park.

variations: Spelling can change in some plurals, so learners should store high-frequency irregular forms as vocabulary.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Countable and uncountable nouns: basics
records.objective: Distinguish common count and mass nouns in simple contexts.

concept.en: Countable nouns can be counted as separate items and have singular/plural forms; uncountable nouns are normally treated as a mass and do not use a/an or a regular plural in their basic meaning.
concept.vi: Danh từ đếm được có thể đếm thành từng đơn vị và có dạng số ít/số nhiều; danh từ không đếm được thường được xem như một khối và không dùng a/an hay dạng số nhiều thông thường trong nghĩa cơ bản.

formulae: countable: a/an + singular noun; number + plural noun
whenToUse: Choose articles and quantity words that match whether a noun is countable.
Treat common mass nouns such as water, rice and information as uncountable in basic use.

positive: I need an apple and some water.
We bought two chairs for the room.
She gave me some useful information.

variations: Some nouns can be countable or uncountable with different meanings; this A1 topic focuses on their most common basic use.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Some and any: basics
records.objective: Use some and any in simple affirmative, negative and question contexts.

concept.en: Use some mainly in affirmative statements and any mainly in negatives and questions when talking about an unspecified quantity or number.
concept.vi: Dùng some chủ yếu trong câu khẳng định và any chủ yếu trong câu phủ định hoặc câu hỏi khi nói về số lượng không xác định.

formulae: negative: not ... any + plural count/uncountable noun
whenToUse: Talk about an unspecified amount or number.
Ask whether an amount or number exists.

positive: We have some eggs in the fridge.
question: Do you have any questions?

variations: Some is also common in offers and requests such as Would you like some water?, but the basic A1 contrast is affirmative some vs negative/question any.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Have/has for possession
records.objective: Express possession and basic relationships with have/has.

concept.en: Use have with I/you/we/they and has with he/she/it to say that someone owns, possesses or has a relationship with something or someone.
concept.vi: Dùng have với I/you/we/they và has với he/she/it để diễn tả sự sở hữu, có một vật, hoặc có một mối quan hệ với ai đó.

whenToUse: Talk about possessions.
Talk about family, features and other simple relationships.

positive: I have a new phone.
Maya has two brothers.
Our apartment has a small balcony.

variations: In standard Present Simple questions and negatives, use do/does: Do you have...? / She does not have....

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Possessive 's
records.objective: Show ownership and relationships with noun + ’s.

concept.en: Add 's to a singular noun or name to show ownership or a relationship.
concept.vi: Thêm 's vào danh từ số ít hoặc tên riêng để thể hiện sự sở hữu hoặc mối quan hệ.

formulae: plural noun ending in -s + ' + possessed noun
whenToUse: Show that something belongs to a person or animal.
Express common relationships such as family or roles.

positive: This is Anna's bag.
My brother's room is upstairs.
The students' books are on the table.

variations: For a regular plural already ending in -s, add only an apostrophe: the students' books.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Simple: facts and states
records.objective: Describe general truths, stable situations and common states.

concept.en: Use the Present Simple for facts, general truths and states that are normally true, not only for repeated routines.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại đơn cho sự thật, chân lý chung và trạng thái thường đúng, không chỉ cho thói quen lặp lại.

formulae: Subject + base verb (+ s/es with he/she/it).
whenToUse: State facts and general truths.
Describe stable situations, preferences or knowledge.

positive: Water boils at 100°C at sea level.
My parents live in Hanoi.
She likes quiet cafés.

variations: State verbs such as know, like and want are commonly used in the Present Simple for basic state meanings.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Simple: third-person -s
records.objective: Form he/she/it verb forms accurately.

concept.en: In affirmative Present Simple clauses, add -s or -es to the main verb when the subject is he, she, it or a singular noun.
concept.vi: Trong câu khẳng định ở Hiện tại đơn, thêm -s hoặc -es vào động từ chính khi chủ ngữ là he, she, it hoặc danh từ số ít.

formulae: consonant + y: y → ies in common verbs such as study → studies
whenToUse: Make affirmative Present Simple verbs agree with a third-person singular subject.

positive: He works near the station.
Mina watches the news at night.
My sister studies English every day.

variations: After does or does not, use the base verb: Does he work? / He does not work.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Simple: negatives
records.objective: Use don't/doesn't + base verb.

concept.en: Use don't with I/you/we/they and doesn't with he/she/it to make negative Present Simple statements; keep the main verb in the base form.
concept.vi: Dùng don't với I/you/we/they và doesn't với he/she/it để tạo câu phủ định ở Hiện tại đơn; động từ chính giữ nguyên dạng cơ bản.

whenToUse: Say that a routine, fact, preference or state is not true.
Contrast a negative Present Simple statement with an affirmative one.

negative: I don't drink coffee after dinner.
They don't live near the station.

variations: Do not add third-person -s after doesn't: she doesn't work, not she doesn't works.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Simple: yes/no questions
records.objective: Form Do/Does questions and short answers.

concept.en: Use do before I/you/we/they and does before he/she/it to make Present Simple yes/no questions; use the base form of the main verb.
concept.vi: Dùng do trước I/you/we/they và does trước he/she/it để tạo câu hỏi yes/no ở Hiện tại đơn; động từ chính dùng dạng cơ bản.

formulae: Yes, subject + do/does. / No, subject + don't/doesn't.
whenToUse: Ask whether a routine, fact, preference or state is true.
Give a short yes/no answer without repeating the full clause.

question: Do you walk to work every day?
Does Leo play tennis after school?
Do they need a ticket for this bus?

variations: After does, use the base verb: Does she live here?, not Does she lives here?

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Simple: wh- questions
records.objective: Ask for basic information with who/what/where/when/why/how.

concept.en: Put a wh-word before a Present Simple question to ask for specific information such as place, time, reason or manner.
concept.vi: Đặt từ để hỏi trước câu hỏi ở Hiện tại đơn để hỏi thông tin cụ thể như nơi chốn, thời gian, lý do hoặc cách thức.

whenToUse: Ask for a missing piece of basic information.
Ask about routines, facts and regular activities.

question: Where do you buy your groceries?
What does Maya do after class?
When do the shops close?

variations: When who or what is the subject, do/does may not appear; that subject-question pattern is treated separately from this basic object/adverbial pattern.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Adverbs of frequency
records.objective: Place always/usually/often/sometimes/never naturally.

concept.en: Frequency adverbs such as always, usually, often, sometimes and never normally go before a main verb but after the verb be.
concept.vi: Trạng từ tần suất như always, usually, often, sometimes và never thường đứng trước động từ thường nhưng đứng sau động từ be.

whenToUse: Say how often a routine or repeated action happens.
Describe how often a state with be is true.

positive: I usually eat breakfast at home.
She is often busy on Monday mornings.
We never watch TV during dinner.

variations: Sometimes can also appear at the beginning or end of a clause, but the mid-position pattern is the core A1 rule.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Can/can't: ability
records.objective: Talk about present ability and inability.

concept.en: Use can + base verb for present ability and can't/cannot + base verb for present inability.
concept.vi: Dùng can + động từ nguyên mẫu để nói về khả năng hiện tại và can't/cannot + động từ nguyên mẫu để nói về việc không có khả năng.

whenToUse: Say what someone is able or unable to do now.
Ask about a person's present ability.

positive: I can swim across the pool.
negative: My little brother can't ride a bike yet.
question: Can you use this camera?

variations: Can does not change with he/she/it, and the following verb stays in the base form.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Can: permission and simple requests
records.objective: Ask for permission and make simple requests with can.

concept.en: Use Can I...? to ask for permission and Can you...? to make a simple request; can can also give basic permission.
concept.vi: Dùng Can I...? để xin phép và Can you...? để đưa ra yêu cầu đơn giản; can cũng có thể dùng để cho phép ở mức cơ bản.

whenToUse: Ask whether you may do something.
Ask another person to do something simple.
Give basic permission.

question: Can I open the window?
Can you help me with this bag, please?
positive: You can use my phone if you need it.

variations: Please can make a request sound friendlier, but can is still less formal than could or may.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Imperatives and instructions
records.objective: Give simple commands, directions and instructions.

concept.en: Use the base verb without an expressed subject for a simple command or instruction; use don't + base verb for a negative imperative.
concept.vi: Dùng động từ dạng cơ bản mà không cần nêu chủ ngữ để đưa ra mệnh lệnh hoặc hướng dẫn đơn giản; dùng don't + động từ cơ bản cho câu mệnh lệnh phủ định.

whenToUse: Give simple directions or instructions.
Ask someone to do or not do something directly.

positive: Please close the door quietly.
Turn left at the next corner.

variations: Please can soften a direct instruction; the grammatical verb form remains the base form.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Object pronouns
records.objective: Use me/you/him/her/it/us/them after verbs and prepositions.

concept.en: Use object pronouns such as me, him, her, us and them when the pronoun receives the action or follows a preposition.
concept.vi: Dùng đại từ tân ngữ như me, him, her, us và them khi đại từ nhận tác động của hành động hoặc đứng sau giới từ.

whenToUse: Replace a known person or thing after a verb.
Use the correct pronoun after a preposition.

positive: Please call me after work.
I see her at the gym every morning.
The teacher gives us homework every Friday.

variations: You and it have the same subject and object forms; the other common personal pronouns change form.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Likes and dislikes with nouns and -ing forms
records.objective: Talk about simple likes and dislikes with nouns and -ing forms.

concept.en: Use like, love, enjoy and hate with a noun or an -ing form to talk about preferences.
concept.vi: Dùng like, love, enjoy và hate với danh từ hoặc dạng -ing để nói về sở thích.

whenToUse: Talk about things or activities you like or dislike.
Ask and answer simple questions about preferences.

positive: I like coffee.
Mina loves reading after dinner.
We enjoy playing board games.

variations: With he, she and it in the present simple, use likes, loves, enjoys or hates.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Want and need + to-infinitive
records.objective: Use want to and need to for simple wishes and necessities.

concept.en: Use want to + base verb for wishes and need to + base verb for necessities.
concept.vi: Dùng want to + động từ nguyên mẫu để nói mong muốn và need to + động từ nguyên mẫu để nói điều cần thiết.

whenToUse: Say what you would like to do.
Say what is necessary to do.

positive: I want to learn Spanish.
He needs to leave early.
We want to visit the museum.

variations: With he, she and it in the present simple, use wants to and needs to.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Time prepositions: at, on and in
records.objective: Use at, on and in for basic times, days, dates and longer periods.

concept.en: Use at for clock times, on for days and dates, and in for months, years and longer periods.
concept.vi: Dùng at cho giờ cụ thể, on cho ngày/ngày tháng và in cho tháng, năm hoặc khoảng thời gian dài hơn.

whenToUse: Say when an event happens.
Give simple schedule and calendar information.

positive: The class starts at nine.
We meet on Friday.
My birthday is in July.

variations: Common fixed expressions include at night, in the morning and on Monday morning.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Place prepositions: in, on, at, under and next to
records.objective: Describe simple locations with common place prepositions.

concept.en: Use common place prepositions to show where a person or thing is.
concept.vi: Dùng các giới từ chỉ nơi chốn thông dụng để nói người hoặc vật đang ở đâu.

whenToUse: Describe where objects are.
Give simple location information about people and places.

positive: The keys are on the table.
Sam is at the bus stop.
The bag is under the chair.

variations: Use in for an enclosed area, on for a surface, and at for a point or specific place.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Movement prepositions: to, into, out of and from
records.objective: Use basic prepositions to describe movement between places.

concept.en: Use to for a destination, into for movement inside, out of for movement from inside, and from for a starting point.
concept.vi: Dùng to cho điểm đến, into cho chuyển động vào bên trong, out of cho chuyển động ra khỏi bên trong và from cho điểm xuất phát.

whenToUse: Say where someone is going.
Describe simple movement into or out of a place.

positive: We walk to school.
She goes into the shop.
They come from Hanoi.

variations: Do not normally use to before home after go/come: go home, come home.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Adjective position before nouns and after be
records.objective: Put common adjectives in the correct position in simple sentences.

concept.en: Put an adjective before a noun, or after be when the adjective describes the subject.
concept.vi: Đặt tính từ trước danh từ, hoặc sau động từ be khi tính từ miêu tả chủ ngữ.

whenToUse: Describe people, places and things.
Add simple information about size, colour, quality or feeling.

positive: It is a small room.
The room is small.
She has a blue bag.

variations: English adjectives do not change for singular or plural nouns: a small room, two small rooms.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Degree words: very and really
records.objective: Use very and really to strengthen simple adjectives and preferences.

concept.en: Use very before many adjectives, and use really before adjectives or common preference verbs to add emphasis.
concept.vi: Dùng very trước nhiều tính từ và really trước tính từ hoặc các động từ chỉ sở thích thông dụng để nhấn mạnh.

whenToUse: Make a simple description stronger.
Emphasize a preference.

positive: The film is very funny.
This bag is really heavy.
I really like this song.

variations: Do not use very directly before a verb: say I really like it, not I very like it.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Basic coordinators: and, but and or
records.objective: Connect simple words and clauses with and, but and or.

concept.en: Use and to add information, but to show contrast, and or to present a choice.
concept.vi: Dùng and để thêm thông tin, but để thể hiện sự tương phản và or để đưa ra lựa chọn.

whenToUse: Join two related ideas.
Show a simple contrast.
Offer or ask about alternatives.

positive: I like tea and coffee.
The room is small but comfortable.
Do you want rice or noodles?

variations: In short A1 sentences, a comma is usually unnecessary before and, but or or when they join words or short phrases.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Because for simple reasons
records.objective: Give a direct reason with because.

concept.en: Use because before a clause that gives the reason for something.
concept.vi: Dùng because trước một mệnh đề để nêu lý do trực tiếp cho một việc.

whenToUse: Give a simple reason for an action, feeling or situation.
Answer a basic why-question.

positive: I stayed home because I was tired.
We are happy because the test is easy.
Because it is raining, we need umbrellas.

variations: Because introduces the reason; so introduces the result.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Continuous: temporary situations
records.objective: Describe short-term situations around now.

concept.en: Use the Present Continuous for temporary situations happening around the present time, even if not happening this exact second.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại tiếp diễn cho tình huống tạm thời đang diễn ra trong khoảng thời gian hiện tại, dù không nhất thiết đúng ngay giây đang nói.

whenToUse: Describe a temporary living, working or study situation.
Talk about a short-term change around now.

positive: I am staying with my aunt this week.
Leo is working from home this month.
They are taking a short course this summer.

variations: Temporary Present Continuous contrasts with Present Simple for usual or permanent situations.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Simple vs Present Continuous: basic contrast
records.objective: Choose routine/state vs action-in-progress meanings.

concept.en: Use the Present Simple for routines, facts and states; use the Present Continuous for actions happening now or temporary situations.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại đơn cho thói quen, sự thật và trạng thái; dùng Hiện tại tiếp diễn cho hành động đang xảy ra hoặc tình huống tạm thời.

whenToUse: Choose between a usual action and an action happening now.
Contrast a regular situation with a temporary one.

positive: I usually take the bus, but today I am walking.
She works in Hanoi, but this month she is working in Da Nang.

variations: State verbs such as know and like usually use the Present Simple, not the Present Continuous.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Was/were
records.objective: Describe past states, identity and location.

concept.en: Use was with I/he/she/it and were with you/we/they to talk about past states, identity and location.
concept.vi: Dùng was với I/he/she/it và were với you/we/they để nói về trạng thái, danh tính hoặc vị trí trong quá khứ.

whenToUse: Describe where someone was in the past.
Describe a past state or condition.

positive: I was at home yesterday.
They were tired after the trip.
Was she at school this morning?

variations: Negative forms are was not/wasn't and were not/weren't.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Past Simple: regular verbs
records.objective: Form and use regular past verbs for finished events.

concept.en: Use the Past Simple of regular verbs, usually formed with -ed, for finished actions in the past.
concept.vi: Dùng Quá khứ đơn của động từ có quy tắc, thường thêm -ed, cho hành động đã kết thúc trong quá khứ.

whenToUse: Talk about a finished action yesterday, last week or at another finished past time.
Tell simple past events in sequence.

positive: We visited the museum yesterday.
She cleaned her room last night.
They played football after school.

variations: Spelling changes include live → lived, study → studied and stop → stopped.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Past Simple: common irregular verbs
records.objective: Use high-frequency irregular past forms in finished events.

concept.en: Some common verbs have irregular Past Simple forms that do not use -ed, such as go → went and see → saw.
concept.vi: Một số động từ thông dụng có dạng Quá khứ đơn bất quy tắc không thêm -ed, như go → went và see → saw.

whenToUse: Talk about finished past events with common irregular verbs.
Describe simple past experiences and actions.

positive: We went to the park.
I saw an old friend.
She had breakfast at seven.

variations: Learn high-frequency irregular forms as fixed verb pairs: go/went, see/saw, have/had, get/got.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Past Simple: negatives and questions
records.objective: Use didn't + base verb and Did...?

concept.en: Use did not/didn't + base verb for Past Simple negatives and Did + subject + base verb for questions.
concept.vi: Dùng did not/didn't + động từ nguyên mẫu cho câu phủ định Quá khứ đơn và Did + chủ ngữ + động từ nguyên mẫu cho câu hỏi.

whenToUse: Say that a past action did not happen.
Ask whether a past action happened.

positive: I didn't call yesterday.
Did she finish the book?
Did they go by bus?

variations: After did or didn't, use the base form: did go, didn't see, not did went or didn't saw.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Be going to: intentions and plans
records.objective: Talk about plans and intentions already decided.

concept.en: Use be going to + base verb for a future plan or intention that is already decided.
concept.vi: Dùng be going to + động từ nguyên mẫu cho kế hoạch hoặc ý định tương lai đã được quyết định.

formulae: Subject + am/is/are going to + base verb.
whenToUse: Talk about a personal plan already decided.
Say what someone intends to do soon.

positive: I am going to study tonight.
She is going to visit her aunt.
We are going to cook at home.

variations: Use the correct form of be before going to: am/is/are.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Will: simple predictions and immediate decisions
records.objective: Use will for basic predictions and decisions made at the moment.

concept.en: Use will + base verb for a simple prediction or a decision made at the moment of speaking.
concept.vi: Dùng will + động từ nguyên mẫu cho dự đoán đơn giản hoặc quyết định được đưa ra ngay lúc nói.

whenToUse: Make a simple prediction about the future.
Make an immediate decision, offer or promise.

positive: I think it will rain tomorrow.
I will carry that bag for you.
We won't be late.

variations: Will is often shortened to 'll in speech and informal writing.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Would like: wants, offers and invitations
records.objective: Use would like for polite wants and simple offers/invitations.

concept.en: Use would like for a polite want, and would you like for simple offers and invitations.
concept.vi: Dùng would like để diễn đạt mong muốn lịch sự và would you like cho lời mời hoặc đề nghị đơn giản.

formulae: Subject + would like + to + base verb.
Would you like + noun/to + base verb?
whenToUse: Ask for something politely.
Offer food or drink, or invite someone to do something.

positive: I would like some water.
She would like to sit down.
Would you like to come with us?

variations: I'd like is the common contraction of I would like.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Basic English sentence order
records.objective: Build clear SVO clauses and place basic time/place information naturally.

concept.en: A basic English statement usually follows subject + verb + object, with common place and time information after the core clause.
concept.vi: Câu trần thuật tiếng Anh cơ bản thường theo thứ tự chủ ngữ + động từ + tân ngữ; thông tin nơi chốn và thời gian thường đứng sau phần chính của câu.

whenToUse: Build clear basic statements.
Put simple place and time expressions in a natural order.

positive: Maya reads books.
We play football in the park on Sundays.
He drinks coffee at home every morning.

variations: English word order is less flexible than Vietnamese in many basic statements; keep the subject before the main verb.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A1 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Past Simple with finished time
records.objective: Link completed past events to finished time expressions.

concept.en: Use the Past Simple for an action completed at a finished time in the past.
concept.vi: Dùng Quá khứ đơn cho hành động đã hoàn tất tại một thời điểm quá khứ đã kết thúc.

whenToUse: Use it with times such as yesterday, last night, in 2024 or two days ago.

positive: I finished the report yesterday.
Sara called me last night.
We moved here in 2024.

variations: A finished-time expression normally selects the Past Simple.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Past Continuous: background actions
records.objective: Set the scene with actions in progress at a past time.

concept.en: Use the Past Continuous to describe an activity or situation in progress around a past time.
concept.vi: Dùng Quá khứ tiếp diễn để mô tả hoạt động hoặc tình huống đang diễn ra quanh một thời điểm trong quá khứ.

whenToUse: Set the background scene for another past event or describe what was happening at a stated past time.

positive: It was raining while we were driving home.
The children were playing outside at six.
I was reading when the lights went out.

variations: The Past Continuous presents an action as in progress rather than as a completed event.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Past Continuous + Past Simple: interruption
records.objective: Describe an action in progress interrupted by a shorter event.

concept.en: Use the Past Continuous for an action already in progress and the Past Simple for the shorter event that interrupts it.
concept.vi: Dùng Quá khứ tiếp diễn cho hành động đang diễn ra và Quá khứ đơn cho sự kiện ngắn chen vào.

whenToUse: Describe an interrupted past activity.

positive: I was cooking when the phone rang.
They were walking home when it started to snow.
She was sleeping when the alarm went off.

variations: When commonly introduces the shorter interrupting event.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Past Simple vs Past Continuous
records.objective: Choose completed events vs background/in-progress past actions.

concept.en: Choose the Past Simple for completed events and the Past Continuous for activities in progress at that past moment.
concept.vi: Chọn Quá khứ đơn cho sự kiện hoàn tất và Quá khứ tiếp diễn cho hoạt động đang diễn ra tại thời điểm quá khứ đó.

whenToUse: Contrast a background activity with a completed event in a past story.

positive: I was taking a shower when you called.
While Ben was driving, he saw an accident.
We were having dinner when the power went out.

variations: While often introduces the longer background action.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Used to: past habits and states
records.objective: Describe past habits/states that are no longer true.

concept.en: Use used to + base verb for past habits or states that are no longer true now.
concept.vi: Dùng used to + động từ nguyên mẫu cho thói quen hoặc trạng thái trong quá khứ hiện nay không còn đúng.

formulae: Subject + didn't use to + base verb.
whenToUse: Talk about repeated past habits or old situations that changed.

positive: I used to live near the sea.
Mina used to walk to school.
We didn't use to have a car.

variations: Used to describes a past pattern, not a single finished event.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Perfect: recent events and present result
records.objective: Connect a recent past event to a current result.

concept.en: Use the Present Perfect when a recent past action has an important result now.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại hoàn thành khi một hành động vừa xảy ra trong quá khứ tạo ra kết quả quan trọng ở hiện tại.

whenToUse: Connect a recent action with its present result.

positive: I've lost my keys, so I can't open the door.
Leo has broken his glasses, so he can't read clearly.
We've finished the work, so we can go home.

variations: The present result is more important than the exact past time.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Perfect with ever/never
records.objective: Ask and answer about experience with ever and never.

concept.en: Use ever in Present Perfect questions and never in statements to talk about experience up to now.
concept.vi: Dùng ever trong câu hỏi Hiện tại hoàn thành và never trong câu khẳng định để nói về trải nghiệm tính đến hiện tại.

whenToUse: Ask about or state life experience without a finished past time.

positive: Have you ever ridden a horse?
I've never flown in a helicopter.
Has Tom ever tried sushi?

variations: Never already contains a negative meaning, so do not add not.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Perfect with already/yet
records.objective: Express earlier-than-expected completion and pending completion.

concept.en: Use already for something completed sooner than expected and yet mainly in Present Perfect questions and negatives.
concept.vi: Dùng already cho việc đã hoàn tất sớm hơn dự kiến và yet chủ yếu trong câu hỏi hoặc phủ định ở Hiện tại hoàn thành.

whenToUse: Talk about whether an expected action is complete by now.

positive: I've already sent the email.
Nina hasn't finished yet.
Have they arrived yet?

variations: Already normally comes before the past participle; yet usually comes at the end.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Perfect with just
records.objective: Describe very recent completed events.

concept.en: Use just with the Present Perfect for an action completed a very short time ago.
concept.vi: Dùng just với Hiện tại hoàn thành cho hành động vừa mới hoàn tất cách đây rất ngắn.

whenToUse: Report very recent news or actions.

positive: I've just eaten lunch.
The train has just left.
Mia has just called me.

variations: In standard British-style usage, just commonly appears with the Present Perfect.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Perfect with since/for
records.objective: Express duration from a starting point or over a period.

concept.en: Use since for a starting point and for for a duration with a situation continuing up to now.
concept.vi: Dùng since cho mốc bắt đầu và for cho khoảng thời gian khi tình huống kéo dài đến hiện tại.

formulae: have/has + past participle + since + starting point
whenToUse: Say how long a current situation has continued.

positive: I've lived here for three years.
She has worked here since May.
They've known each other for a long time.

variations: Use since with points such as Monday, 2024 or I was a child.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple: basic contrast
records.objective: Choose unspecified/current relevance vs finished past time.

concept.en: Use the Present Perfect for an unfinished time or experience connected to now, and the Past Simple with a finished past time.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại hoàn thành cho khoảng thời gian chưa kết thúc hoặc trải nghiệm liên quan hiện tại; dùng Quá khứ đơn với thời gian quá khứ đã kết thúc.

formulae: Past Simple: past form + finished-time expression
whenToUse: Choose between present relevance and a specific finished past event.

positive: I've visited Hue twice.
I visited Hue last summer.
Have you seen this film? I saw it yesterday.

variations: Do not combine the Present Perfect with explicit finished times such as yesterday or last year.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Much, many and a lot of
records.objective: Choose quantity expressions for countable and uncountable nouns.

concept.en: Use many with countable plural nouns, much with uncountable nouns, and a lot of with both in common affirmative sentences.
concept.vi: Dùng many với danh từ đếm được số nhiều, much với danh từ không đếm được và a lot of với cả hai trong nhiều câu khẳng định thông dụng.

whenToUse: Talk about large quantities and ask how much or how many.

positive: How many books do you have?
We don't have much time.
There are a lot of people here.

variations: Much is less common than a lot of in affirmative informal statements.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: A few/few and a little/little
records.objective: Express positive or insufficient small quantities.

concept.en: Use a few with countable plural nouns and a little with uncountable nouns for small but positive amounts.
concept.vi: Dùng a few với danh từ đếm được số nhiều và a little với danh từ không đếm được để chỉ lượng nhỏ nhưng vẫn có.

whenToUse: Describe small quantities without meaning zero.

positive: I have a few questions.
There is a little milk left.
We have a few minutes before class.

variations: Few/little without a usually sound more negative: almost not enough.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Some/any/no/every compounds
records.objective: Use someone/anything/nothing/everywhere and related forms.

concept.en: Use indefinite pronouns such as someone, anyone, everyone, something and nothing when the exact person or thing is not named.
concept.vi: Dùng đại từ bất định như someone, anyone, everyone, something và nothing khi không nêu chính xác người hoặc vật.

formulae: some- forms often in affirmative statements
every-/no- forms for all or none
whenToUse: Refer to unspecified people, things or places.

positive: Someone is at the door.
I didn't see anyone in the room.
Everything is ready.

variations: Indefinite pronouns normally take a singular verb: Everyone is ready.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Comparative adjectives and adverbs
records.objective: Compare two people, things or actions.

concept.en: Use comparative adjectives with than to compare two people, things or situations.
concept.vi: Dùng tính từ so sánh hơn với than để so sánh hai người, vật hoặc tình huống.

whenToUse: Compare two items by one quality.

positive: This bag is cheaper than that one.
My sister is taller than me.
This chair is more comfortable than that chair.

variations: Some common comparatives are irregular, such as good → better and bad → worse.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Superlatives
records.objective: Identify the highest/lowest degree in a group.

concept.en: Use the superlative to identify the highest or lowest degree within a group.
concept.vi: Dùng so sánh nhất để chỉ mức độ cao nhất hoặc thấp nhất trong một nhóm.

whenToUse: Compare one member with a group of three or more.

positive: Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
This is the easiest question on the page.
Mia is the most careful driver in our family.

variations: Irregular forms include best and worst.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: As...as and not as...as
records.objective: Express equality and inequality.

concept.en: Use as + adjective/adverb + as to say two things are equal, and not as ... as to show inequality.
concept.vi: Dùng as + tính từ/trạng từ + as để nói hai đối tượng ngang nhau và not as ... as để nói không ngang nhau.

whenToUse: Compare equality or difference without using -er/more.

positive: This room is as quiet as the library.
My phone isn't as expensive as yours.
Tom runs as fast as Ben.

variations: As ... as can compare adjectives or adverbs.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Too and enough with adjectives/adverbs
records.objective: Express excess and sufficiency.

concept.en: Use too + adjective for more than is acceptable and adjective + enough for a sufficient degree.
concept.vi: Dùng too + tính từ cho mức độ quá mức và tính từ + enough cho mức độ đủ.

whenToUse: Explain why something is impossible, difficult or possible because of degree.

positive: This box is too heavy to carry.
The water is warm enough to swim in.
He isn't old enough to drive.

variations: Too usually expresses an excessive, often problematic degree.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Too much/too many/enough + noun
records.objective: Express excess or sufficiency with nouns.

concept.en: Use too much with uncountable nouns, too many with plural countable nouns, and enough before nouns for sufficient quantity.
concept.vi: Dùng too much với danh từ không đếm được, too many với danh từ đếm được số nhiều và enough trước danh từ để chỉ lượng đủ.

whenToUse: Judge whether a quantity is excessive or sufficient.

positive: There is too much sugar in this tea.
We have too many bags.
There aren't enough chairs for everyone.

variations: Enough comes before a noun but after an adjective.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Will: predictions
records.objective: Make neutral predictions about the future.

concept.en: Use will + base verb for a prediction based mainly on opinion, belief or expectation.
concept.vi: Dùng will + động từ nguyên mẫu cho dự đoán chủ yếu dựa trên ý kiến, niềm tin hoặc kỳ vọng.

formulae: Subject + probably will / will probably + base verb.
whenToUse: Make general future predictions when there is no present visible evidence.

positive: I think our team will win.
It will probably rain this evening.
People will use less paper in the future.

variations: Expressions such as I think, probably and maybe often accompany predictions.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Going to: evidence-based predictions
records.objective: Predict a near future result based on present evidence.

concept.en: Use be going to for a prediction based on present evidence that you can see or know now.
concept.vi: Dùng be going to cho dự đoán dựa trên bằng chứng hiện tại mà ta có thể thấy hoặc biết ngay lúc này.

formulae: Subject + am/is/are going to + base verb.
whenToUse: Predict a likely near-future event from visible present evidence.

positive: Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.
Be careful! You're going to drop that glass.
The baby is yawning; she's going to fall asleep.

variations: Going to can express both prior intentions and evidence-based predictions.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Continuous: future arrangements
records.objective: Talk about personal arrangements already organized.

concept.en: Use the Present Continuous for a future arrangement that has already been organized, often with a specific time or person.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại tiếp diễn cho một sắp xếp tương lai đã được tổ chức, thường có thời gian hoặc người liên quan cụ thể.

whenToUse: Talk about fixed personal arrangements such as meetings, visits or travel.

positive: I'm meeting Ana at six.
We're having dinner with Sam tomorrow.
They are flying to Bangkok on Friday.

variations: A future time expression makes the future meaning clear.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Simple: timetables and schedules
records.objective: Use present simple for fixed future schedules.

concept.en: Use the Present Simple for timetables and fixed public schedules.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại đơn cho thời khóa biểu, lịch trình và giờ cố định được công bố.

formulae: Scheduled subject + Present Simple + future time.
whenToUse: State train, bus, film, class or event times that are fixed by a schedule.

positive: The train leaves at 7:30 tomorrow.
The film starts at eight.
Our class finishes at noon.

variations: This use is common for transport and official timetables.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Future forms: plans, arrangements, schedules and predictions
records.objective: Choose among going to, present continuous, present simple and will.

concept.en: Choose going to for prior intentions, Present Continuous for arranged plans, Present Simple for schedules and will for opinion-based predictions or immediate decisions.
concept.vi: Chọn going to cho ý định đã có, Hiện tại tiếp diễn cho sắp xếp đã chốt, Hiện tại đơn cho lịch trình và will cho dự đoán theo ý kiến hoặc quyết định tức thời.

whenToUse: Select a basic future form according to meaning rather than using one future form for every situation.

positive: I'm going to study medicine after school.
I'm meeting the teacher at three tomorrow.
I think the test will be difficult.

variations: The same future event can sometimes be framed differently depending on intention, arrangement or prediction.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Can/could: present and past ability
records.objective: Contrast present ability with general past ability.

concept.en: Use could or couldn't to describe general ability in the past.
concept.vi: Dùng could hoặc couldn't để nói về khả năng chung trong quá khứ.

whenToUse: Say what someone was generally able or unable to do at an earlier age or period.

positive: I could swim when I was five.
She couldn't read before she started school.
Could you ride a bike at six?

variations: For one successful event, later levels often prefer was/were able to rather than could.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Must and have to: obligation
records.objective: Express internal/external obligation in common contexts.

concept.en: Use must for strong speaker-imposed necessity and have to for necessity caused by rules or circumstances.
concept.vi: Dùng must cho sự bắt buộc mạnh do người nói nhấn mạnh và have to cho sự bắt buộc do quy định hoặc hoàn cảnh.

whenToUse: Express obligation and necessity in everyday rules and situations.

positive: You must wear a seat belt.
I have to start work at eight.
We had to wait outside.

variations: Past necessity is normally expressed with had to, not must.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Mustn't vs don't have to
records.objective: Distinguish prohibition from lack of necessity.

concept.en: Use mustn't for prohibition and don't/doesn't have to for lack of necessity.
concept.vi: Dùng mustn't cho điều bị cấm và don't/doesn't have to cho điều không bắt buộc.

formulae: don't/doesn't have to + base verb = not necessary
whenToUse: Distinguish something forbidden from something optional.

positive: You mustn't touch that wire.
You don't have to come early.
Students mustn't use phones during the test.

variations: The two negative-looking forms have very different meanings.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Should/shouldn't: advice
records.objective: Give and ask for everyday advice.

concept.en: Use should or shouldn't + base verb to give or ask for advice.
concept.vi: Dùng should hoặc shouldn't + động từ nguyên mẫu để đưa ra hoặc hỏi lời khuyên.

whenToUse: Recommend a sensible action without expressing a strict rule.

positive: You should drink more water.
He shouldn't stay up so late.
Should I call the doctor?

variations: Should gives advice; must expresses stronger obligation.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: May/might: possibility
records.objective: Express uncertain present or future possibilities.

concept.en: Use may or might + base verb to say something is possible but not certain.
concept.vi: Dùng may hoặc might + động từ nguyên mẫu để nói điều gì đó có thể xảy ra nhưng không chắc chắn.

whenToUse: Express uncertain present or future possibility.

positive: It may rain later.
Sara might be at home.
We might not finish today.

variations: At A2, may and might can usually be treated as similar markers of possibility.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Could/may: polite requests and permission
records.objective: Make more polite requests and ask/give permission.

concept.en: Use could/can for polite requests and may/can for asking permission, with could and may often sounding more formal.
concept.vi: Dùng could/can cho lời nhờ lịch sự và may/can để xin phép; could và may thường trang trọng hơn.

whenToUse: Ask someone to do something or ask permission politely.

positive: Could you open the window, please?
May I use your phone?
Can I sit here?

variations: Please can be added to requests; may is common for more formal permission.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Zero Conditional
records.objective: Describe general truths, rules and repeated cause-effect.

concept.en: Use the Zero Conditional for facts, routines and results that are generally true whenever the condition happens.
concept.vi: Dùng Câu điều kiện loại 0 cho sự thật, thói quen và kết quả thường đúng mỗi khi điều kiện xảy ra.

whenToUse: State general truths, instructions or repeated cause-and-effect relationships.

positive: If you heat ice, it melts.
If I don't sleep enough, I feel tired.
Plants die if they don't get water.

variations: Both clauses normally use the Present Simple because the result is general, not a one-time future prediction.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Future time clauses with when/as soon as/until
records.objective: Use present forms after future time conjunctions.

concept.en: Use a present tense after when, after, before, until and as soon as to refer to the future; use will in the main clause when needed.
concept.vi: Dùng thì hiện tại sau when, after, before, until và as soon as để nói về tương lai; dùng will ở mệnh đề chính khi cần.

whenToUse: Describe the timing of future actions.

positive: I'll call you when I arrive.
We'll eat after Dad gets home.
Please wait here until the bus comes.

variations: The main clause may use will, an imperative or another suitable future form.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: To-infinitive for purpose
records.objective: Explain why someone does something using to + verb.

concept.en: Use to + base verb to explain the purpose of an action.
concept.vi: Dùng to + động từ nguyên mẫu để giải thích mục đích của một hành động.

whenToUse: Answer the question why someone does something.

positive: I went to the shop to buy milk.
She called me to ask a question.
We use this box to store tools.

variations: For + noun can express purpose too, but for + base verb is not the same construction.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Common verb + to-infinitive patterns
records.objective: Use want/hope/plan/decide/need and similar verbs with to-infinitives.

concept.en: Some common verbs such as want, decide, hope, plan and need are followed by to + base verb.
concept.vi: Một số động từ thông dụng như want, decide, hope, plan và need được theo sau bởi to + động từ nguyên mẫu.

whenToUse: Use the correct complement after common verbs that select the to-infinitive.

positive: I want to learn Spanish.
They decided to leave early.
Mia hopes to find a new job.

variations: Verb patterns must be learned with the verb because different verbs select different complements.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Common verb + -ing patterns
records.objective: Use enjoy/finish/avoid/mind and similar verbs with -ing.

concept.en: Some common verbs such as enjoy, finish and avoid are followed by an -ing form.
concept.vi: Một số động từ thông dụng như enjoy, finish và avoid được theo sau bởi dạng V-ing.

whenToUse: Use the correct complement after common verbs that select an -ing form.

positive: I enjoy cooking at home.
Leo finished cleaning the kitchen.
They avoid driving at night.

variations: Learn the complement as part of each verb pattern.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Adjective + to-infinitive
records.objective: Use common adjective complements such as happy to/helpful to/easy to.

concept.en: Use adjective + to-infinitive after many adjectives to describe feelings, reactions, difficulty or readiness.
concept.vi: Dùng tính từ + to-infinitive sau nhiều tính từ để nói về cảm xúc, phản ứng, độ khó hoặc sự sẵn sàng.

whenToUse: Add an action after adjectives such as happy, easy, ready, surprised and difficult.

positive: I'm happy to help.
This book is easy to understand.
We were surprised to see Ben.

variations: The adjective describes the subject or the situation, while the infinitive names the related action.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Preposition + -ing
records.objective: Use gerunds after common prepositions.

concept.en: After a preposition, use a noun or an -ing form rather than a to-infinitive.
concept.vi: Sau giới từ, dùng danh từ hoặc dạng V-ing thay vì to-infinitive.

whenToUse: Use verbs after prepositions such as at, for, without, before and after.

positive: She's good at drawing.
Thank you for helping me.
He left without saying goodbye.

variations: To can be a preposition in some patterns, but this A2 rule covers ordinary prepositions such as for and without.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Basic phrasal verbs and object position
records.objective: Place noun/pronoun objects correctly with common separable phrasal verbs.

concept.en: With separable phrasal verbs, a noun object may go before or after the particle, but a pronoun object normally goes between the verb and particle.
concept.vi: Với cụm động từ có thể tách, tân ngữ danh từ có thể đứng trước hoặc sau tiểu từ, nhưng tân ngữ đại từ thường phải đứng giữa động từ và tiểu từ.

formulae: verb + noun + particle / verb + particle + noun
whenToUse: Place noun and pronoun objects correctly with common separable phrasal verbs.

positive: Please turn the light off.
Please turn it off.
She picked the children up at four.

variations: Not every phrasal verb is separable, so object position must be learned with the verb.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Defining relative clauses: who/which/that
records.objective: Add essential information about people and things.

concept.en: Use who for people and that/which for things in a defining relative clause that identifies the noun.
concept.vi: Dùng who cho người và that/which cho vật trong mệnh đề quan hệ xác định để nhận diện danh từ.

whenToUse: Add essential information that tells exactly which person or thing you mean.

positive: A mechanic is a person who repairs cars.
This is the book that I bought yesterday.
The woman who lives next door is a nurse.

variations: That can often refer to people or things in defining clauses, while who is the clearest choice for people.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Relative clauses with where
records.objective: Describe places with where clauses.

concept.en: Use where in a defining relative clause to identify a place by what happens there.
concept.vi: Dùng where trong mệnh đề quan hệ xác định để nhận diện một nơi thông qua việc xảy ra ở đó.

whenToUse: Combine a place noun with information about activities or events at that place.

positive: This is the cafe where we first met.
I know a park where children can play safely.
That's the hotel where we stayed.

variations: Where can often be paraphrased with in/at which at higher levels.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Articles: generic vs specific reference
records.objective: Choose a/an, the or plural reference in common generic/specific contexts.

concept.en: Use a/an when introducing one non-specific singular countable noun and the when both speaker and listener can identify the specific noun.
concept.vi: Dùng a/an khi giới thiệu một danh từ đếm được số ít chưa xác định và the khi cả người nói lẫn người nghe có thể xác định danh từ cụ thể.

formulae: first/non-specific mention: a/an + singular countable noun
whenToUse: Move from introducing something to referring back to the same specific thing.

positive: I saw a dog. The dog was very friendly.
She bought a book. The book is on the table.
We need a taxi. The taxi outside is free.

variations: Specificity depends on shared context, not only on whether a noun was mentioned earlier.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Zero article with plural and uncountable nouns
records.objective: Make generic statements without an article where appropriate.

concept.en: Use no article with plural countable nouns and uncountable nouns when talking about things in general.
concept.vi: Không dùng mạo từ với danh từ đếm được số nhiều và danh từ không đếm được khi nói chung về một loại hoặc khái niệm.

whenToUse: Make general statements about categories, substances and abstract ideas.

positive: Dogs need regular exercise.
Milk is good for children.
Life can be surprising.

variations: Use the when the plural or uncountable noun is made specific by context.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: One/ones as substitutes
records.objective: Avoid repetition by substituting one/ones for count nouns.

concept.en: Use one or ones to avoid repeating a countable noun that is already clear from context.
concept.vi: Dùng one hoặc ones để tránh lặp lại danh từ đếm được đã rõ từ ngữ cảnh.

whenToUse: Compare or choose among previously mentioned countable things without repeating the noun.

positive: I like the red bag, not the blue one.
These shoes are small; I need bigger ones.
Which cake do you want? The chocolate one.

variations: One/ones replace countable nouns, not uncountable nouns.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Reflexive pronouns
records.objective: Use myself/yourself/etc. when subject and object refer to the same participant.

concept.en: Use reflexive pronouns when the subject and object refer to the same person or group, or for emphasis.
concept.vi: Dùng đại từ phản thân khi chủ ngữ và tân ngữ cùng chỉ một người/nhóm, hoặc để nhấn mạnh.

formulae: I → myself, you → yourself/yourselves, he → himself, she → herself, we → ourselves, they → themselves
whenToUse: Show that an action returns to the subject or emphasize who did it without help.

positive: I cut myself while cooking.
They made the cake themselves.
She taught herself to play the guitar.

variations: Reflexive pronouns are not used simply because the subject is a person; they need a reflexive or emphatic function.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Adverbs of manner
records.objective: Describe how actions happen and form common -ly adverbs.

concept.en: Use an adverb of manner to describe how an action happens; many are formed by adding -ly to an adjective.
concept.vi: Dùng trạng từ chỉ cách thức để mô tả một hành động diễn ra như thế nào; nhiều trạng từ được tạo bằng cách thêm -ly vào tính từ.

whenToUse: Describe the manner of speaking, moving, working or doing another action.

positive: She speaks English clearly.
The baby slept quietly.
Please drive carefully.

variations: Some adverbs are irregular or unchanged, such as well and fast.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Adjective vs adverb
records.objective: Choose the correct form to modify nouns, verbs and adjectives.

concept.en: Use adjectives to describe nouns or follow linking verbs, and adverbs to modify ordinary action verbs.
concept.vi: Dùng tính từ để mô tả danh từ hoặc sau động từ nối; dùng trạng từ để bổ nghĩa cho động từ hành động thông thường.

whenToUse: Choose between a quality of a person/thing and the manner of an action.

positive: Mia is a careful driver.
Mia drives carefully.
The test was easy, and I finished it quickly.

variations: Linking verbs such as be, seem and feel normally take adjectives rather than manner adverbs.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Because, so, although and while
records.objective: Connect clauses for reason, result, contrast and simultaneous situations.

concept.en: Use basic subordinators such as because, although, before, after and when to connect a main clause with a dependent clause.
concept.vi: Dùng các liên từ phụ thuộc cơ bản như because, although, before, after và when để nối mệnh đề chính với mệnh đề phụ.

whenToUse: Express reason, contrast, time and sequence with two related clauses.

positive: I stayed home because I was sick.
Although it was cold, we went for a walk.
I called Sam before I left.

variations: A comma is common when the dependent clause comes first.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Basic question tags
records.objective: Use common positive/negative tag patterns to check information.

concept.en: Use a short question tag with the opposite polarity of the statement to check or confirm information.
concept.vi: Dùng câu hỏi đuôi ngắn có tính khẳng định/phủ định ngược với mệnh đề chính để kiểm tra hoặc xác nhận thông tin.

whenToUse: Seek confirmation in simple statements with be, auxiliaries and common modal verbs.

positive: It's cold today, isn't it?
You like coffee, don't you?
She can swim, can't she?

variations: The tag repeats the auxiliary or modal from the statement when one is present.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled A2 grammar-body scale content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Perfect: unfinished time periods
records.objective: Talk about events within time periods that continue to now.
