concept.en: Use the Present Perfect for actions in a time period that has not finished yet.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại hoàn thành cho hành động xảy ra trong một khoảng thời gian vẫn chưa kết thúc.

formulae: Subject + have/has + past participle + unfinished-time expression.
whenToUse: Use expressions such as today, this week or this year when that period is still continuing.

positive: I've answered five emails today.
Mina has read three chapters this week.
We've had two meetings this month.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Perfect: repeated events up to now
records.objective: Describe repeated actions whose time frame includes the present.

concept.en: Use the Present Perfect for repeated events up to now when the time period remains open.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại hoàn thành cho các sự kiện lặp lại tính đến hiện tại khi khoảng thời gian vẫn còn mở.

formulae: Subject + have/has + past participle + number/frequency expression.
whenToUse: Count repeated experiences or events from the past up to the present.

positive: We've visited that cafe four times.
She has called me twice today.
I've seen that film three times.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Perfect: result focus vs event focus
records.objective: Choose wording based on whether the current result or occurrence matters.

concept.en: Use the Present Perfect to focus on a present result and the Past Simple to tell a finished past event.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại hoàn thành để nhấn mạnh kết quả hiện tại và Quá khứ đơn để kể một sự kiện đã kết thúc trong quá khứ.

whenToUse: Choose the tense according to whether the focus is the current result or the past event itself.

positive: I've lost my wallet, so I can't pay.
I lost my wallet on the bus yesterday.
She's broken her arm, so she can't drive.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Been vs gone
records.objective: Distinguish returned experience/location from still-being-away meaning.

concept.en: Use has/have been to mean someone went somewhere and returned; use has/have gone when the person is still away.
concept.vi: Dùng has/have been khi ai đó đã đi đâu và đã quay về; dùng has/have gone khi người đó vẫn đang ở nơi khác.

formulae: have/has been to + place = visited and returned
have/has gone to + place = went and is still there
whenToUse: Distinguish completed visits from a person's current absence.

positive: Lena has been to Japan twice.
Tom has gone to the bank; he'll be back soon.
Have you ever been to Singapore?

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Have had and other state verbs over time
records.objective: Use present perfect with possession and long-running states.

concept.en: Use have/has had with for or since when possession or a state began in the past and continues now.
concept.vi: Dùng have/has had với for hoặc since khi việc sở hữu hay trạng thái bắt đầu trong quá khứ và vẫn tiếp tục đến hiện tại.

whenToUse: Describe how long a current possession, relationship or state has lasted.

positive: I've had this laptop for three years.
Sara has had that job since June.
We've had the same teacher since September.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present Perfect Continuous: duration
records.objective: Emphasize ongoing/recent activity over a period leading to now.

concept.en: Use the Present Perfect Continuous to emphasize the duration of an activity that began in the past and continues or has just stopped.
concept.vi: Dùng Hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn để nhấn mạnh thời lượng của một hoạt động bắt đầu trong quá khứ và vẫn tiếp tục hoặc vừa mới dừng.

whenToUse: Focus on how long an activity has been in progress.

positive: I've been studying for two hours.
It has been raining since morning.
They've been waiting for the bus for thirty minutes.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Past Perfect: earlier past
records.objective: Mark an event as earlier than another past reference point.

concept.en: Use the Past Perfect for an event completed before another past event or past reference point.
concept.vi: Dùng Quá khứ hoàn thành cho một sự kiện đã hoàn tất trước một sự kiện hay mốc khác trong quá khứ.

whenToUse: Make the earlier of two past events clear.

positive: The train had left before we reached the station.
By the time I arrived, the meeting had started.
She was tired because she hadn't slept well.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Past Perfect vs Past Simple
records.objective: Use past perfect only when earlier-past ordering needs marking.

concept.en: Use the Past Perfect for the earlier event and the Past Simple for the later event in a past sequence when the order needs clarification.
concept.vi: Dùng Quá khứ hoàn thành cho sự kiện xảy ra trước và Quá khứ đơn cho sự kiện xảy ra sau khi cần làm rõ thứ tự trong quá khứ.

whenToUse: Clarify the order of two completed past events.

positive: After we had eaten, we went for a walk.
When I got home, everyone had gone to bed.
She had finished the report before the manager called.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Narrative tenses
records.objective: Combine past simple, continuous and perfect to tell coherent stories.

concept.en: Combine Past Simple, Past Continuous and Past Perfect to show main events, background actions and earlier events in a story.
concept.vi: Kết hợp Quá khứ đơn, Quá khứ tiếp diễn và Quá khứ hoàn thành để thể hiện sự kiện chính, hành động nền và sự kiện xảy ra trước trong một câu chuyện.

whenToUse: Organize a past narrative so the timeline and background are clear.

positive: I was walking home when I noticed I had lost my keys.
The sun was shining when we left the hotel.
She opened the door and saw that someone had moved the box.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Used to vs would for past habits
records.objective: Choose forms for repeated past actions and past states.

concept.en: Use used to for repeated past habits and past states; use would for repeated past actions, but not normally for past states.
concept.vi: Dùng used to cho thói quen lặp lại và trạng thái trong quá khứ; dùng would cho hành động lặp lại trong quá khứ nhưng thường không dùng cho trạng thái.

formulae: used to + base verb = past habit/state
would + base verb = repeated past action
whenToUse: Choose between two ways of describing repeated past behavior.

positive: We used to live near the station.
Every summer, we would visit our grandparents.
She used to have long hair.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Future Continuous
records.objective: Describe actions expected to be in progress at a future time.

concept.en: Use the Future Continuous for an action that will be in progress at a particular future time.
concept.vi: Dùng Tương lai tiếp diễn cho hành động sẽ đang diễn ra tại một thời điểm cụ thể trong tương lai.

whenToUse: Describe an activity expected to be in progress around a future time.

positive: This time tomorrow, I'll be flying to Hanoi.
At eight, we'll be having dinner.
Don't call at ten; I'll be sleeping.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Will vs going to: intention and prediction nuance
records.objective: Choose between spontaneous/neutral future meaning and prior intention/evidence.

concept.en: Use will for decisions made now and opinion-based predictions; use be going to for prior intentions and evidence-based predictions.
concept.vi: Dùng will cho quyết định tức thời và dự đoán dựa trên ý kiến; dùng be going to cho ý định đã có và dự đoán dựa trên bằng chứng hiện tại.

whenToUse: Choose the future form according to decision timing and evidence.

positive: I'll answer the phone.
I'm going to start a course next month.
Look at those clouds; it's going to rain.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present forms for future events
records.objective: Distinguish arrangements from fixed schedules in realistic planning.

concept.en: Use present and future forms according to whether a future event is a timetable, arrangement, intention, prediction or action in progress.
concept.vi: Chọn các dạng hiện tại và tương lai tùy theo sự kiện là lịch trình, sắp xếp, ý định, dự đoán hay hành động đang diễn ra trong tương lai.

whenToUse: Select a more precise future form from context.

positive: The train leaves at 6:20.
I'm meeting Lee after work.
At nine tomorrow, I'll be taking my exam.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: First Conditional: modal and imperative results
records.objective: Use can/may/might/should or imperatives in realistic result clauses.

concept.en: In First Conditional patterns, the result clause can use will, can, may, might or an imperative depending on the intended result.
concept.vi: Trong câu điều kiện loại 1, mệnh đề kết quả có thể dùng will, can, may, might hoặc câu mệnh lệnh tùy ý nghĩa.

formulae: If + Present Simple, will/can/may/might + base verb.
whenToUse: Express likely results, possibilities, permission or instructions after a realistic future condition.

positive: If you finish early, you can leave.
If it rains, we might stay home.
If you see Mia, tell her to call me.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Unless, as long as and provided that
records.objective: Express conditions without relying only on if.

concept.en: Use unless, as long as, provided/providing and in case to express different kinds of conditions and precautions.
concept.vi: Dùng unless, as long as, provided/providing và in case để diễn đạt các loại điều kiện và biện pháp đề phòng khác nhau.

formulae: as long as/provided = only if condition is met
in case = precaution for a possible situation
whenToUse: Vary conditional linking words while keeping their meanings distinct.

positive: You won't pass unless you study.
You can borrow the car as long as you're careful.
Take an umbrella in case it rains.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Wish + past: present wishes
records.objective: Express dissatisfaction with a present situation.

concept.en: Use wish + Past Simple to talk about a present situation that you want to be different.
concept.vi: Dùng wish + Quá khứ đơn để nói về một tình huống hiện tại mà bạn muốn nó khác đi.

formulae: wish + could + base verb for present ability/possibility
whenToUse: Express regret or dissatisfaction about an unreal present situation.

positive: I wish I lived closer to work.
She wishes she had more free time.
I wish I could speak Japanese.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Hope vs wish
records.objective: Choose realistic desired outcomes vs counterfactual/regret meanings.

concept.en: Use hope for a real or possible situation and wish for an unreal, regretted or desired different situation.
concept.vi: Dùng hope cho tình huống có thật hoặc có khả năng xảy ra và wish cho điều không thực, đáng tiếc hoặc mong muốn khác với thực tế.

formulae: wish + Past Simple for unreal present
whenToUse: Distinguish realistic hopes from wishes about unreal situations.

positive: I hope the weather is good tomorrow.
I wish I had more free time.
We hope you can come to the party.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Must/might/can't: present deduction
records.objective: Infer present situations with different confidence levels.

concept.en: Use must for a strong positive deduction and can't for a strong negative deduction about the present.
concept.vi: Dùng must cho suy đoán khẳng định rất chắc và can't cho suy đoán phủ định rất chắc về hiện tại.

whenToUse: Make logical conclusions from present evidence.

positive: The lights are on, so Maya must be home.
That can't be Ben; he's abroad.
You worked all night, so you must be tired.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: May/might/could: degrees and contexts of possibility
records.objective: Express uncertain possibilities with natural modal choices.

concept.en: Use may, might and could to express present or future possibility with uncertainty.
concept.vi: Dùng may, might và could để diễn tả khả năng ở hiện tại hoặc tương lai nhưng không chắc chắn.

whenToUse: Show that something is possible rather than certain.

positive: We might go out later.
The answer could be correct.
Mina may not come tonight.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Have to, must and need to
records.objective: Distinguish sources and strengths of obligation/necessity.

concept.en: Use must, have to and need to for necessity, and don't need to or don't have to when something is not necessary.
concept.vi: Dùng must, have to và need to cho sự cần thiết; dùng don't need to hoặc don't have to khi điều gì đó không cần thiết.

formulae: don't need to/don't have to + base verb
whenToUse: Express different everyday kinds of obligation and lack of necessity.

positive: You need to bring your passport.
We have to leave by six.
You don't need to print the form.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Should, ought to and had better
records.objective: Adjust the strength and consequence implied by advice.

concept.en: Use should or ought to for normal advice and had better for stronger advice with a possible negative consequence.
concept.vi: Dùng should hoặc ought to cho lời khuyên thông thường và had better cho lời khuyên mạnh hơn khi có thể có hậu quả xấu.

whenToUse: Choose the strength of advice according to the situation.

positive: You should get more sleep.
You ought to talk to your manager.
You'd better take an umbrella; the sky is very dark.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Can/could/be allowed to
records.objective: Express permission across present, past and more formal contexts.

concept.en: Use can/could/may for permission and be allowed to when another tense or form is needed.
concept.vi: Dùng can/could/may để nói hoặc xin phép và be allowed to khi cần một thì hoặc dạng khác.

whenToUse: Talk about permission in present, past and future contexts.

positive: You can use my laptop.
We weren't allowed to enter the room.
Will visitors be allowed to take photos?

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Gerund vs infinitive after verbs with little meaning change
records.objective: Use common verbs that accept both patterns naturally.

concept.en: Some verbs such as like, love, hate, start and begin can take either an -ing form or a to-infinitive with little change in basic meaning.
concept.vi: Một số động từ như like, love, hate, start và begin có thể đi với V-ing hoặc to-infinitive mà nghĩa cơ bản thay đổi rất ít.

whenToUse: Recognize common verbs that accept both complement patterns.

positive: I like reading before bed.
I like to read before bed.
It started raining after lunch.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Remember/forget + -ing vs to-infinitive
records.objective: Distinguish memory of past action from remembering a duty.

concept.en: Remember/forget + to-infinitive refers to remembering or forgetting a necessary action; remember/forget + -ing refers to a memory of an earlier event.
concept.vi: Remember/forget + to-infinitive nói về việc nhớ hoặc quên làm một việc cần làm; remember/forget + V-ing nói về ký ức của một việc đã xảy ra.

formulae: remember/forget to do = action still to perform
remember/forget doing = memory of past event
whenToUse: Distinguish a duty from a memory.

positive: Remember to lock the door.
I remember meeting her years ago.
He forgot to send the email.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Stop/try + -ing vs to-infinitive
records.objective: Distinguish ending an activity, purpose, experiment and effort meanings.

concept.en: Stop + -ing means end an activity, stop + to-infinitive means pause another activity in order to do something; try + -ing tests a method, while try + to-infinitive attempts a difficult action.
concept.vi: Stop + V-ing nghĩa là chấm dứt một hoạt động, stop + to-infinitive là dừng việc khác để làm việc này; try + V-ing là thử một phương pháp, còn try + to-infinitive là cố gắng thực hiện.

whenToUse: Choose gerund or infinitive when the meaning changes.

positive: He stopped smoking last year.
We stopped to buy some water.
Try restarting the computer.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Verb + object + to-infinitive
records.objective: Use tell/ask/want/allow/encourage patterns.

concept.en: Many verbs such as ask, tell, want, expect and advise can be followed by an object plus a to-infinitive.
concept.vi: Nhiều động từ như ask, tell, want, expect và advise có thể theo sau bởi tân ngữ + to-infinitive.

whenToUse: Report requests, expectations, instructions and advice directed at another person.

positive: She asked me to wait outside.
The doctor advised him to rest.
We expect them to arrive soon.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Make/let/help + object + verb
records.objective: Use causative/permission patterns with bare infinitives appropriately.

concept.en: Use make and let with object + bare infinitive; help can take object + bare infinitive or to-infinitive.
concept.vi: Dùng make và let với tân ngữ + động từ nguyên mẫu không to; help có thể đi với tân ngữ + động từ nguyên mẫu có hoặc không có to.

whenToUse: Express causing, permitting or assisting another person to do something.

positive: The joke made us laugh.
My parents let me stay out late.
She helped me carry the boxes.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Passive Voice: present and past simple
records.objective: Shift focus from doer to action/result.

concept.en: Form the present and past passive with the correct form of be plus a past participle when the action or result is more important than the agent.
concept.vi: Tạo câu bị động hiện tại và quá khứ bằng dạng thích hợp của be + quá khứ phân từ khi hành động hoặc kết quả quan trọng hơn người thực hiện.

formulae: Present Simple passive: am/is/are + past participle
Past Simple passive: was/were + past participle
whenToUse: Shift focus from who does an action to what receives the action.

positive: English is spoken in many countries.
The bridge was built in 1998.
These rooms are cleaned every day.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Passive with modal verbs
records.objective: Form modal + be + past participle for rules, possibility and obligation.

concept.en: Form a passive after a modal with modal + be + past participle.
concept.vi: Tạo câu bị động sau động từ khuyết thiếu bằng modal + be + quá khứ phân từ.

whenToUse: Express rules, possibilities, duties or abilities when the receiver of the action is the focus.

positive: The form must be signed.
Tickets can be bought online.
The problem should be fixed soon.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Passive agents and when to omit them
records.objective: Decide whether a by-agent is useful, obvious or irrelevant.

concept.en: In passive sentences, include by + agent only when the agent is important, informative or surprising; omit it when unknown or obvious.
concept.vi: Trong câu bị động, chỉ thêm by + tác nhân khi người thực hiện quan trọng, cung cấp thông tin hoặc đáng chú ý; bỏ đi khi không biết hoặc đã hiển nhiên.

formulae: passive clause (+ by + agent when useful)
whenToUse: Decide whether naming the agent adds meaningful information.

positive: My bike was stolen last night.
The novel was written by George Orwell.
The road is being repaired.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Defining relative clauses
records.objective: Add essential identifying information accurately.

concept.en: Use defining relative clauses to give essential information that identifies the person, thing or place being discussed.
concept.vi: Dùng mệnh đề quan hệ xác định để cung cấp thông tin thiết yếu giúp xác định người, vật hoặc nơi đang nói đến.

whenToUse: Identify exactly which noun you mean without commas.

positive: The woman who called earlier is my manager.
I need the file that you sent yesterday.
That's the cafe where we met.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Non-defining relative clauses
records.objective: Add extra information with commas and appropriate pronouns.

concept.en: Use non-defining relative clauses between commas to add extra information about a noun that is already identified.
concept.vi: Dùng mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định, đặt giữa dấu phẩy, để thêm thông tin phụ về danh từ đã được xác định rõ.

whenToUse: Add non-essential background information without changing which noun is meant.

positive: My brother, who lives in Da Nang, is visiting us.
This laptop, which I bought last year, is already broken.
Hanoi, which is Vietnam's capital, has many lakes.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Omitting relative pronouns
records.objective: Omit object relative pronouns when grammar allows it.

concept.en: In a defining relative clause, omit who/that/which when it is the object, but not when it is the subject.
concept.vi: Trong mệnh đề quan hệ xác định, có thể lược bỏ who/that/which khi nó là tân ngữ, nhưng không lược bỏ khi nó là chủ ngữ.

whenToUse: Recognize when a relative pronoun can be omitted naturally.

positive: The book I bought is excellent.
The person we met was friendly.
The woman who works here is helpful.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Relative clauses with whose
records.objective: Express possession inside defining and non-defining relative clauses.

concept.en: Use whose in a relative clause to show possession or relationship.
concept.vi: Dùng whose trong mệnh đề quan hệ để thể hiện sở hữu hoặc mối quan hệ.

whenToUse: Link a person or thing to something that belongs to or is associated with it.

positive: I met a woman whose son is a pilot.
That's the company whose office moved downtown.
Students whose work is late must email the teacher.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Reported statements
records.objective: Report speech with pronoun/time changes and basic backshift.

concept.en: Report what someone said by using a reporting verb plus a statement clause, often with tense and reference changes when reporting later.
concept.vi: Tường thuật lời nói của ai đó bằng động từ tường thuật + mệnh đề, thường có thay đổi thì và từ chỉ thời gian/người khi kể lại sau đó.

whenToUse: Report statements without repeating the speaker's exact words.

positive: Mia said that she was tired.
Tom told me that he needed help.
They said they would call later.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Reported questions
records.objective: Use statement word order in reported yes/no and wh-questions.

concept.en: Report questions with statement word order and no do/does/did auxiliary; use if/whether for yes-no questions.
concept.vi: Tường thuật câu hỏi bằng trật tự câu khẳng định và không dùng trợ động từ do/does/did; dùng if/whether cho câu hỏi yes-no.

whenToUse: Turn direct questions into reported questions.

positive: She asked where I lived.
He asked if I was ready.
They asked what time the train left.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Reported requests and commands
records.objective: Report instructions using tell/ask + object + to-infinitive.

concept.en: Report requests and commands with ask/tell/order + object + to-infinitive, and use not to for negative commands.
concept.vi: Tường thuật lời yêu cầu và mệnh lệnh bằng ask/tell/order + tân ngữ + to-infinitive; dùng not to cho mệnh lệnh phủ định.

formulae: tell + object + not to + base verb
whenToUse: Report what someone asked or ordered another person to do.

positive: She asked me to sit down.
The teacher told us to be quiet.
Dad told me not to stay out late.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Reported speech: backshift vs unchanged truth
records.objective: Choose when backshift is natural and when it is unnecessary.

concept.en: When reporting past speech later, present forms often backshift to past forms and will often changes to would, unless the information is still current or backshift is unnecessary.
concept.vi: Khi tường thuật lại lời nói trong quá khứ, các thì hiện tại thường lùi về quá khứ và will thường đổi thành would, trừ khi thông tin vẫn còn đúng hoặc không cần lùi thì.

whenToUse: Show the time relationship between the original speech and the later report.

positive: 'I'm busy.' → She said she was busy.
'I'll call.' → He said he would call.
'I can swim.' → Mia said she could swim.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Indirect questions
records.objective: Use polite question frames with statement word order.

concept.en: Use introductory phrases such as Could you tell me or Do you know followed by statement word order in the question clause.
concept.vi: Dùng các cụm mở đầu như Could you tell me hoặc Do you know, sau đó dùng trật tự câu khẳng định trong mệnh đề hỏi.

whenToUse: Ask questions more politely or indirectly.

positive: Could you tell me where the station is?
Do you know if the shop is open?
Can you tell me what time it starts?

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Question tags: agreement and intonation meaning
records.objective: Form tags and understand checking vs confirmation functions.

concept.en: Form question tags by matching the auxiliary or modal in the statement and reversing positive/negative polarity.
concept.vi: Tạo câu hỏi đuôi bằng cách dùng cùng trợ động từ hoặc modal của mệnh đề chính và đảo tính khẳng định/phủ định.

whenToUse: Check information or invite agreement with a wider range of tenses and auxiliaries.

positive: You've met Sara, haven't you?
He didn't call, did he?
They can come, can't they?

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Embedded wh-clauses
records.objective: Use wh-clauses after verbs such as know, wonder and explain.

concept.en: Use an embedded question as a noun-like clause after verbs or expressions such as know, wonder, remember or I'm not sure, with statement word order.
concept.vi: Dùng câu hỏi lồng như một mệnh đề danh từ sau các động từ/cụm như know, wonder, remember hoặc I'm not sure, với trật tự câu khẳng định.

whenToUse: Put a question meaning inside a larger statement rather than asking directly.

positive: I don't know where he lives.
I wonder whether they have arrived.
I'm not sure what this button does.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Comparative modifiers
records.objective: Use much/far/a lot/a bit/slightly with comparatives.

concept.en: Use words such as much, far, a lot, a bit and slightly before comparative forms to show the size of the difference.
concept.vi: Dùng các từ như much, far, a lot, a bit và slightly trước dạng so sánh hơn để thể hiện mức độ chênh lệch.

whenToUse: Make comparisons more precise by indicating a large or small difference.

positive: This route is much faster.
The blue room is slightly bigger than the green one.
Her new job is a lot more interesting.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Same as, different from and similar to
records.objective: Express comparison relationships with correct prepositions.

concept.en: Use the same as, different from and similar to to express equality, difference and similarity between things.
concept.vi: Dùng the same as, different from và similar to để diễn tả sự giống nhau, khác nhau và tương tự giữa các đối tượng.

whenToUse: Compare relationships without using ordinary comparative adjectives.

positive: My answer is the same as yours.
This design is different from the old one.
Her bag is similar to mine.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Too/enough: consequence and implication
records.objective: Use too/enough to imply whether an action/result is possible.

concept.en: Use too to show an excessive degree that causes a problem and enough to show sufficient degree or quantity; their position differs with adjectives and nouns.
concept.vi: Dùng too để chỉ mức độ quá mức gây vấn đề và enough để chỉ mức độ/số lượng đủ; vị trí của enough khác nhau với tính từ và danh từ.

whenToUse: Explain whether a degree or amount prevents or allows an action.

positive: The box is too heavy for me to lift.
She's experienced enough to lead the team.
We have enough chairs for everyone.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: So and such
records.objective: Intensify adjective/adverb vs noun phrases correctly.

concept.en: Use so before an adjective/adverb and such before a noun phrase to emphasize degree or introduce a result.
concept.vi: Dùng so trước tính từ/trạng từ và such trước cụm danh từ để nhấn mạnh mức độ hoặc dẫn tới một kết quả.

whenToUse: Choose the correct intensifier according to whether a noun phrase follows.

positive: The film was so good that I watched it twice.
It was such a good film that I watched it twice.
She spoke so quietly that I couldn't hear.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Articles with institutions and activities
records.objective: Distinguish school/work/home/bed as activities vs specific places.

concept.en: With institutions such as school, university, prison, hospital and bed, article choice can distinguish their normal purpose from the physical place or a specific building.
concept.vi: Với các từ chỉ cơ sở như school, university, prison, hospital và bed, lựa chọn mạo từ có thể phân biệt chức năng thông thường với địa điểm/vật cụ thể.

formulae: go to school/bed/prison for normal function
go to the school/bed/building when referring to a specific place/object
whenToUse: Choose zero article or the according to institutional function versus specific reference.

positive: The children are at school.
I went to the school to meet the teacher.
It's late, so I'm going to bed.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Articles with geographical names
records.objective: Use the/zero article with countries, rivers, seas, mountains and regions.

concept.en: Use the with certain geographical names such as rivers, seas, oceans, deserts and plural country/group names, but usually no article with cities, most countries, lakes and individual mountains.
concept.vi: Dùng the với một số tên địa lý như sông, biển, đại dương, sa mạc và tên quốc gia/nhóm ở dạng số nhiều; thường không dùng mạo từ với thành phố, đa số quốc gia, hồ và núi riêng lẻ.

whenToUse: Apply common article patterns to geographical names.

positive: The Nile flows through several countries.
Japan is in Asia.
Mount Fuji is in Japan.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Both/either/neither
records.objective: Refer to two people or things with correct agreement and meaning.

concept.en: Use both for two together, either for one of two, and neither for not one and not the other.
concept.vi: Dùng both cho cả hai, either cho một trong hai và neither cho không cái nào trong hai.

whenToUse: Refer precisely to a set of two people or things.

positive: Both answers are correct.
You can take either bus.
Neither option is cheap.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Each, every and all
records.objective: Choose distributive vs group reference.

concept.en: Use each to focus on members individually, every for all members considered one by one, and all for the whole group or quantity.
concept.vi: Dùng each để nhấn từng thành viên riêng lẻ, every cho tất cả thành viên xét từng người/vật, và all cho toàn bộ nhóm hoặc lượng.

formulae: all + plural countable or uncountable noun
whenToUse: Choose a quantifier according to individual versus collective focus.

positive: Each student has a locker.
Every room has a window.
All students need an ID card.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Another/other/others/the other
records.objective: Refer to additional and remaining people/things accurately.

concept.en: Use another for one more singular item, other before plural/uncountable nouns, the other for the remaining specific one, and others as a pronoun.
concept.vi: Dùng another cho thêm một vật số ít, other trước danh từ số nhiều/không đếm được, the other cho vật cụ thể còn lại và others như đại từ.

whenToUse: Avoid repeating nouns while distinguishing additional and remaining items.

positive: Can I have another cup?
Some students stayed; others went home.
I have two bags: one is black and the other is blue.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Most, enough and plenty of
records.objective: Express broad proportions and sufficiency naturally.

concept.en: Use most for the majority, enough for a sufficient amount and plenty of for more than enough.
concept.vi: Dùng most cho phần lớn, enough cho lượng đủ và plenty of cho lượng nhiều hơn đủ.

whenToUse: Describe majority, sufficiency and abundance.

positive: Most people use smartphones.
We have enough food for everyone.
There's plenty of time.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Common adjective + preposition patterns
records.objective: Use patterns such as interested in, good at and responsible for.

concept.en: Learn common adjective + preposition combinations as fixed patterns, such as interested in, good at, afraid of and responsible for.
concept.vi: Học các kết hợp tính từ + giới từ thông dụng như interested in, good at, afraid of và responsible for như những mẫu cố định.

whenToUse: Use the preposition selected by a common adjective.

positive: I'm interested in photography.
She's good at solving problems.
Who is responsible for this project?

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Common noun + preposition patterns
records.objective: Use patterns such as reason for, solution to and increase in.

concept.en: Learn common noun + preposition combinations such as reason for, solution to, increase in and relationship with/between.
concept.vi: Học các kết hợp danh từ + giới từ thông dụng như reason for, solution to, increase in và relationship with/between.

whenToUse: Use the conventional preposition that follows common abstract nouns.

positive: What's the reason for the delay?
We need a solution to this problem.
There was an increase in prices.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Common verb + preposition patterns
records.objective: Use depend on, belong to, apply for and similar combinations.

concept.en: Learn common verb + preposition combinations such as depend on, belong to, apologize for and worry about.
concept.vi: Học các kết hợp động từ + giới từ thông dụng như depend on, belong to, apologize for và worry about.

whenToUse: Use the preposition required by common verbs.

positive: It depends on the weather.
This bag belongs to Mia.
He apologized for being late.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Phrasal verbs: separable vs inseparable
records.objective: Place objects correctly and identify particle/preposition behavior.

concept.en: Distinguish separable phrasal verbs, where an object can split verb and particle, from inseparable phrasal verbs, where it cannot.
concept.vi: Phân biệt cụm động từ tách được, nơi tân ngữ có thể đứng giữa động từ và tiểu từ, với cụm không tách được.

formulae: separable: verb + object + particle / verb + particle + noun
whenToUse: Place noun and pronoun objects correctly with different phrasal verbs.

positive: Please turn the radio off.
Please turn it off.
I ran into an old friend yesterday.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Although, despite and in spite of
records.objective: Express concession with correct clause or noun/-ing complements.

concept.en: Use although, even though, though and despite/in spite of to express a contrast between an expected result and what actually happens.
concept.vi: Dùng although, even though, though và despite/in spite of để diễn tả sự tương phản giữa điều được mong đợi và điều thực tế xảy ra.

whenToUse: Connect contrasting ideas with the correct clause or noun pattern.

positive: Although it was raining, we went out.
Despite the rain, we went out.
She finished the race even though she was tired.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Because of, therefore and as a result
records.objective: Connect causes and consequences across sentence structures.

concept.en: Use because/since/as to introduce reasons and so/therefore/as a result to express results, with different punctuation and clause patterns.
concept.vi: Dùng because/since/as để giới thiệu lý do và so/therefore/as a result để diễn tả kết quả, với cách nối câu và dấu câu khác nhau.

formulae: result clause with so / therefore / as a result
whenToUse: Link causes and consequences clearly.

positive: We stayed home because it was raining.
It was raining, so we stayed home.
The road was closed; therefore, we took another route.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Narrative sequencing and discourse markers
records.objective: Organize spoken/written stories with before, after, then, eventually and meanwhile.

concept.en: Use linkers such as first, then, after that, meanwhile, eventually and in the end to organize events and show sequence in a narrative.
concept.vi: Dùng các từ nối như first, then, after that, meanwhile, eventually và in the end để tổ chức sự kiện và thể hiện trình tự trong câu chuyện.

whenToUse: Make a story easier to follow by signaling order and simultaneous events.

positive: First, we checked the map; then we started walking.
Meanwhile, the others were preparing dinner.
Eventually, we found the right path.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B1 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present perfect simple/continuous: nuanced aspect choice
records.objective: Choose completion, result, repetition, temporary activity or duration focus.

concept.en: Perfect forms connect an earlier situation to a later reference point; choose simple or continuous aspect according to result, completion and duration focus.
concept.vi: Các dạng hoàn thành nối một tình huống xảy ra trước với một mốc tham chiếu sau; chọn dạng đơn hay tiếp diễn tùy trọng tâm kết quả, hoàn tất hay thời lượng.

whenToUse: Contrast result/completion with ongoing process across present and past reference points.

positive: I've finished the report, so you can read it now.
I'd been working for hours before I took a break.
She has known him since school.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Past Perfect Continuous
records.objective: Show duration/activity leading up to a past reference point.

concept.en: Use the Past Perfect Continuous to emphasize the duration or repeated nature of an activity continuing up to a past reference point.
concept.vi: Dùng Quá khứ hoàn thành tiếp diễn để nhấn mạnh thời lượng hoặc tính lặp lại của hoạt động kéo dài đến một mốc trong quá khứ.

whenToUse: Explain what had been happening before another past event, especially when duration or visible results matter.

positive: They had been waiting for an hour when the bus arrived.
Her eyes were tired because she'd been reading all night.
We had been living there for six years before we moved.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Future Perfect
records.objective: Describe actions completed by a future deadline/reference point.

concept.en: Use the Future Perfect for an action that will be completed before a specified future time.
concept.vi: Dùng Tương lai hoàn thành cho hành động sẽ hoàn tất trước một mốc tương lai xác định.

formulae: Subject + will have + past participle + by/before future time.
whenToUse: Look forward from now to a future deadline and describe what will already be complete.

positive: By Friday, we'll have finished the project.
She will have left by the time you arrive.
By next year, they will have lived here for a decade.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Future Continuous: expected course and polite inquiry
records.objective: Describe expected ongoing events and ask about plans neutrally.

concept.en: Besides an action in progress, the Future Continuous can describe an expected event as part of a normal course or politely ask about someone's plans.
concept.vi: Ngoài hành động đang diễn ra, Tương lai tiếp diễn còn có thể diễn tả một việc được dự kiến xảy ra theo tiến trình bình thường hoặc hỏi kế hoạch một cách lịch sự.

whenToUse: Describe expected future routines or ask about plans without sounding like a request.

positive: I'll be seeing Marta tomorrow, so I'll give her the message.
Will you be using the car this evening?
They'll be staying with us for a few days.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Future in the past
records.objective: Use would/was going to/was about to for future viewed from a past point.

concept.en: Use would, was/were going to and was/were about to to describe a future event viewed from a past point.
concept.vi: Dùng would, was/were going to và was/were about to để diễn tả một sự kiện tương lai nhìn từ một mốc trong quá khứ.

whenToUse: Report past plans, predictions and events that were still future at the past reference point.

positive: I knew she would call later.
We were going to leave, but the storm started.
He was about to speak when the phone rang.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Advanced future form choice in plans
records.objective: Coordinate intentions, arrangements, schedules, predictions and deadlines.

concept.en: Use future forms strategically to distinguish intentions, arrangements, schedules, forecasts, deadlines and expected ongoing activity.
concept.vi: Dùng các dạng tương lai có chủ đích để phân biệt ý định, sắp xếp, lịch trình, dự báo, hạn hoàn thành và hoạt động dự kiến đang diễn ra.

whenToUse: Choose a future form according to the speaker's perspective on planning and certainty.

positive: We're meeting the supplier at ten.
The conference starts on Monday.
By noon, I'll have sent the final version.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Second Conditional with could/might
records.objective: Express hypothetical ability and uncertain hypothetical results.

concept.en: In unreal or unlikely present/future conditions, the result clause can use would, could or might to express consequence, ability or possibility.
concept.vi: Trong điều kiện không thực hoặc ít khả năng ở hiện tại/tương lai, mệnh đề kết quả có thể dùng would, could hoặc might để diễn tả kết quả, khả năng hay khả năng xảy ra.

formulae: If + Past Simple, would/could/might + base verb.
whenToUse: Vary the result meaning in Second Conditional patterns.

positive: If I had more time, I could learn another language.
If she lived nearer, we might see her more often.
If they offered me the job, I would accept it.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Mixed Conditional: past condition → present result
records.objective: Connect a counterfactual past event to a present consequence.

concept.en: Use a mixed conditional with an unreal past condition and a present result when a different past action would change the situation now.
concept.vi: Dùng câu điều kiện hỗn hợp với điều kiện quá khứ không có thật và kết quả hiện tại khi một hành động quá khứ khác đi sẽ làm thay đổi tình hình bây giờ.

formulae: If + Past Perfect, would + base verb (present result).
whenToUse: Connect a past cause with its imagined present consequence.

positive: If I'd studied medicine, I'd be a doctor now.
If we hadn't missed the train, we'd be home now.
If she had accepted the offer, she would live in Paris now.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Mixed Conditional: present state → past result
records.objective: Connect an unreal present/general condition to a past consequence.

concept.en: Use a mixed conditional with an unreal present state and a past result when a different present characteristic would have changed a past event.
concept.vi: Dùng câu điều kiện hỗn hợp với trạng thái hiện tại không có thật và kết quả quá khứ khi một đặc điểm hiện tại khác đi sẽ làm thay đổi một sự kiện trong quá khứ.

formulae: If + Past Simple, would have + past participle.
whenToUse: Connect a continuing present condition or characteristic with an imagined past consequence.

positive: If I were more organized, I wouldn't have missed the deadline.
If he spoke Spanish, he could have taken that job.
If we lived closer, we would have visited more often.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Wish/if only + past perfect
records.objective: Express regret about past events.

concept.en: Use wish + Past Perfect to express regret that a past event happened differently from what you wanted.
concept.vi: Dùng wish + Past Perfect để diễn tả tiếc nuối vì một sự kiện quá khứ đã xảy ra khác điều mong muốn.

whenToUse: Imagine a different past and express regret about something that can no longer be changed.

positive: I wish I'd studied harder.
She wishes she hadn't said that.
We wish we'd booked earlier.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Wish/if only + would
records.objective: Express desired change or annoyance about controllable behavior.

concept.en: Use wish + would to complain about repeated behavior or a situation you want someone or something to change.
concept.vi: Dùng wish + would để phàn nàn về hành vi lặp lại hoặc tình huống mà bạn muốn người/vật thay đổi.

whenToUse: Express irritation or desire for a future change, especially when the subject is not normally the speaker.

positive: I wish the neighbors would turn the music down.
She wishes her phone would stop ringing.
I wish you wouldn't interrupt me.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Would rather / would sooner
records.objective: Express preferences about one's own or another person's actions.

concept.en: Use would rather + bare infinitive for your preference and would rather + subject + Past Simple for what you prefer another person to do.
concept.vi: Dùng would rather + động từ nguyên mẫu không to cho sở thích của chính mình và would rather + chủ ngữ + Past Simple cho điều bạn muốn người khác làm.

whenToUse: Express preferences about present or future choices.

positive: I'd rather stay home tonight.
I'd rather you came tomorrow.
Would you rather eat now or later?

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Unreal past after It's time / as if / as though
records.objective: Use past forms for remoteness, criticism or unreal comparison.

concept.en: Use a past form after as if/as though to show that a present appearance or comparison is unreal or unlikely.
concept.vi: Dùng dạng quá khứ sau as if/as though để cho thấy một vẻ ngoài hoặc phép so sánh ở hiện tại là không thật hoặc khó xảy ra.

formulae: present verb + as if/as though + Past Simple
as if/as though + were for formal unreal comparison
whenToUse: Describe an unreal present impression rather than a factual comparison.

positive: He talks as if he knew everything.
She spends money as though she were rich.
You look as if you hadn't slept.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Must have/might have/can't have
records.objective: Make deductions about past events with graded certainty.

concept.en: Use must have + past participle for a strong positive deduction about the past and can't/couldn't have + past participle for a strong negative deduction.
concept.vi: Dùng must have + quá khứ phân từ cho suy đoán khẳng định rất chắc về quá khứ và can't/couldn't have + quá khứ phân từ cho suy đoán phủ định rất chắc.

whenToUse: Infer what probably did or did not happen from evidence available now.

positive: She must have forgotten the meeting.
They can't have left already; their car is still here.
He must have been exhausted after the race.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Should have/ought to have
records.objective: Express criticism, regret and unfulfilled expectation.

concept.en: Use should have or ought to have + past participle to criticize a past action or say what would have been better; shouldn't have marks an action that was a mistake.
concept.vi: Dùng should have hoặc ought to have + quá khứ phân từ để phê bình hành động quá khứ hoặc nói điều lẽ ra tốt hơn; shouldn't have chỉ một hành động đã làm nhưng là sai lầm.

whenToUse: Evaluate past behavior after the opportunity has passed.

positive: You should have told me earlier.
I shouldn't have stayed up so late.
They ought to have checked the address.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Could have/might have
records.objective: Express unrealized options and uncertain past possibilities.

concept.en: Use may/might/could have + past participle for uncertain possibilities about what happened in the past.
concept.vi: Dùng may/might/could have + quá khứ phân từ để nói về những khả năng không chắc chắn đã xảy ra trong quá khứ.

whenToUse: Suggest possible explanations for a past event without claiming certainty.

positive: She might have missed the bus.
The email could have gone to spam.
They may have taken a different road.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Needn't have vs didn't need to
records.objective: Distinguish unnecessary action performed vs no necessity.

concept.en: Needn't have + past participle means an unnecessary action was actually done; didn't need to means there was no necessity and does not by itself say whether the action happened.
concept.vi: Needn't have + quá khứ phân từ nghĩa là một hành động không cần thiết nhưng đã thực sự được làm; didn't need to chỉ nói không có sự cần thiết và không tự cho biết hành động có xảy ra hay không.

formulae: needn't have + past participle = did it, unnecessary
didn't need to + base verb = no necessity
whenToUse: Distinguish unnecessary completed actions from lack of obligation.

positive: You needn't have bought any milk; we had plenty.
I didn't need to work yesterday, so I stayed home.
She needn't have rushed; the train was late.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Continuous and perfect passives
records.objective: Use is being done/has been done/had been done appropriately.

concept.en: Build continuous and perfect passives with be being + past participle and have/has/had been + past participle.
concept.vi: Tạo bị động tiếp diễn và hoàn thành bằng be being + quá khứ phân từ và have/has/had been + quá khứ phân từ.

formulae: continuous passive: be + being + past participle
perfect passive: have/has/had + been + past participle
whenToUse: Keep passive focus while expressing an action in progress or already completed relative to a reference point.

positive: The eastbound railway bridge is being repaired after last week's storm.
The documents have been sent.
The room had been cleaned before we arrived.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Get-passive
records.objective: Use get + past participle in natural informal/eventive contexts.

concept.en: Use get + past participle in informal contexts for events that happen to someone or something, often emphasizing change, accident or involvement.
concept.vi: Dùng get + quá khứ phân từ trong ngữ cảnh thân mật cho sự việc xảy đến với ai/vật, thường nhấn mạnh sự thay đổi, tai nạn hoặc sự tham gia.

whenToUse: Use a less formal alternative to be-passive for dynamic events.

positive: My phone got stolen on the train.
They got married last summer.
Be careful not to get hurt.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Have/get something done
records.objective: Describe arranging for another person to perform a service/action.

concept.en: Use have/get + object + past participle when you arrange for another person to perform a service or when something happens to your property.
concept.vi: Dùng have/get + tân ngữ + quá khứ phân từ khi bạn sắp xếp để người khác thực hiện dịch vụ hoặc khi một sự việc xảy ra với tài sản của mình.

whenToUse: Describe services arranged rather than performed personally, and sometimes unwanted experiences.

positive: I had my hair cut yesterday.
We're getting the kitchen painted.
She had her bag stolen on the bus.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Reporting verbs and complement patterns
records.objective: Use admit/deny/suggest/accuse/remind/warn with correct structures.

concept.en: Different reporting verbs select different complement patterns, such as admit doing, promise to do, warn someone not to do and suggest doing/that-clause.
concept.vi: Các động từ tường thuật khác nhau chọn mẫu bổ ngữ khác nhau, như admit doing, promise to do, warn someone not to do và suggest doing/mệnh đề that.

whenToUse: Choose the complement pattern required by the reporting verb.

positive: He admitted taking the money.
She promised to call.
The guide warned us not to touch the plants.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Reported speech: time, place and viewpoint shifts
records.objective: Adjust deictic words and viewpoint beyond simple tense backshift.

concept.en: Advanced reported speech allows selective backshift, changes in modal meaning, and preservation of a tense when the information remains true or the time relationship is already clear.
concept.vi: Tường thuật nâng cao cho phép lùi thì có chọn lọc, thay đổi modal và giữ nguyên thì khi thông tin vẫn đúng hoặc quan hệ thời gian đã rõ.

formulae: no compulsory backshift for still-true/current information
whenToUse: Report speech naturally rather than applying mechanical tense changes in every context.

positive: The teacher said that water boils at 100°C.
Mina said she'd finished the work the day before.
He told me he might be late.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Reporting with infinitive and gerund patterns
records.objective: Choose structures after advise, promise, recommend, apologize and similar verbs.

concept.en: Use infinitive or gerund reporting structures according to the reporting verb and intended meaning, including accuse someone of doing and remind someone to do.
concept.vi: Dùng cấu trúc tường thuật với infinitive hoặc gerund tùy động từ và ý nghĩa, gồm accuse someone of doing và remind someone to do.

whenToUse: Handle reporting patterns that cannot be reduced to a simple that-clause.

positive: She reminded me to lock the door.
They accused him of lying.
He denied breaking the window.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Relative clauses with prepositions
records.objective: Use formal preposition + whom/which and natural stranded-preposition alternatives.

concept.en: In formal relative clauses, a preposition can come before whom or which; in less formal clauses it often stays at the end.
concept.vi: Trong mệnh đề quan hệ trang trọng, giới từ có thể đứng trước whom hoặc which; trong cách nói ít trang trọng hơn nó thường đứng cuối mệnh đề.

whenToUse: Choose formal or neutral relative-clause preposition placement.

positive: The person to whom I spoke was helpful.
The person who I spoke to was helpful.
This is the topic about which we argued.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Present participle clauses
records.objective: Reduce clauses when subjects align and simultaneous/cause meanings are clear.

concept.en: Use an -ing participle clause to reduce a clause when the understood subject is the same and the action is simultaneous, causal or sequential.
concept.vi: Dùng mệnh đề phân từ V-ing để rút gọn mệnh đề khi chủ ngữ ngầm giống nhau và hành động diễn ra đồng thời, có quan hệ nguyên nhân hoặc trình tự.

whenToUse: Make written sentences more compact while keeping the same subject relationship.

positive: Walking home, I saw an old friend.
Knowing the answer, she raised her hand.
Opening the door, he noticed the lights were off.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Past participle clauses
records.objective: Use reduced passive/result clauses accurately.

concept.en: Use a past-participle clause to reduce a passive or state-based clause when the understood subject is the same as the main clause subject.
concept.vi: Dùng mệnh đề quá khứ phân từ để rút gọn mệnh đề bị động hoặc trạng thái khi chủ ngữ ngầm giống với chủ ngữ mệnh đề chính.

whenToUse: Compress passive background information in formal or written style.

positive: Built in 1920, the house needs major repairs.
Surprised by the news, Mina called immediately.
Designed for beginners, the course is easy to follow.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Reduced relative clauses
records.objective: Condense active/passive relative clauses without ambiguity.

concept.en: Reduce some relative clauses with active V-ing, passive past participles or to-infinitives when the meaning remains clear.
concept.vi: Rút gọn một số mệnh đề quan hệ bằng V-ing chủ động, quá khứ phân từ bị động hoặc to-infinitive khi nghĩa vẫn rõ.

formulae: noun + V-ing ... = noun who/which is doing
noun + past participle ... = noun that is/was done
whenToUse: Make noun phrases more concise in written English.

positive: People waiting outside should form a line.
The documents sent yesterday have arrived.
She was the first person to finish.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Emphatic do
records.objective: Add contrastive emphasis to affirmative present/past statements.

concept.en: Use do/does/did before a base verb in affirmative clauses to add contrastive emphasis, especially when correcting or strongly confirming something.
concept.vi: Dùng do/does/did trước động từ nguyên mẫu trong câu khẳng định để thêm nhấn mạnh tương phản, đặc biệt khi đính chính hoặc khẳng định mạnh.

whenToUse: Emphasize that an affirmative statement is genuinely true.

positive: I do understand your concern.
She does work hard.
He did call me yesterday.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Noun clauses with that, whether/if and wh-words
records.objective: Use clauses as objects/complements with correct word order.

concept.en: Use that-, whether/if- and wh-clauses as noun-like complements after verbs, adjectives and some nouns.
concept.vi: Dùng mệnh đề that, whether/if và wh như bổ ngữ mang chức năng danh từ sau động từ, tính từ và một số danh từ.

whenToUse: Express propositions, uncertainty and embedded information as clause complements.

positive: I believe that the plan will work.
We're not sure whether the data is complete.
She explained why the meeting was canceled.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Whoever/whatever/wherever clauses
records.objective: Express free-choice or unknown reference with -ever forms.

concept.en: Use whoever, whatever, wherever, whenever and however to introduce free relative or concessive clauses meaning any person, thing, place, time or way.
concept.vi: Dùng whoever, whatever, wherever, whenever và however để mở đầu mệnh đề tự do hoặc nhượng bộ mang nghĩa bất kỳ người, vật, nơi, lúc hay cách nào.

whenToUse: Refer generally without naming a specific person or thing, or express concession.

positive: Take whatever you need.
Whoever arrives first should open the door.
Wherever you go, keep in touch.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Gerund clauses as subjects and complements
records.objective: Use -ing clauses as noun-like units in formal and everyday English.

concept.en: Use a gerund clause as the subject of a sentence when an activity or action is treated as a concept.
concept.vi: Dùng mệnh đề V-ing làm chủ ngữ khi một hoạt động hay hành động được xem như một khái niệm.

whenToUse: Make an activity the topic of a statement in neutral or formal English.

positive: Working from home saves time.
Learning a language takes patience.
Driving at night can be tiring.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Infinitive clauses after nouns/adjectives and as complements
records.objective: Build compact to-infinitive clause structures with clear understood subjects.

concept.en: Use to-infinitive clauses after adjectives, nouns and verbs or as extraposed subjects to express purpose, evaluation, intention or potential action.
concept.vi: Dùng mệnh đề to-infinitive sau tính từ, danh từ và động từ hoặc trong cấu trúc chủ ngữ giả để diễn tả mục đích, đánh giá, ý định hay hành động tiềm năng.

whenToUse: Build more complex complements around potential or intended actions.

positive: It's important to check the details.
She has a decision to make.
We agreed to meet outside.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Complex noun phrases with postmodification
records.objective: Build noun phrases using prepositional, relative and non-finite modifiers.

concept.en: Complex noun phrases can pack precise information around a head noun by combining premodifiers with prepositional, relative and non-finite postmodifiers.
concept.vi: Cụm danh từ phức có thể nén thông tin chính xác quanh danh từ trung tâm bằng cách kết hợp bổ ngữ trước với cụm giới từ, mệnh đề quan hệ và cấu trúc không chia ở phía sau.

whenToUse: Use compact noun phrases when several details must identify or describe the same referent without creating a chain of short clauses.

positive: The proposal submitted by the research team addresses several unresolved safety concerns.
Students interested in the internship should apply before the end of the month.
The building across from the station has offices on the top three floors.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Articles with abstract nouns
records.objective: Choose zero/a/the as abstract ideas become general, instances or specified concepts.

concept.en: Article choice with abstract nouns depends on whether the idea is general, one instance or a specifically identified concept.
concept.vi: Việc chọn mạo từ với danh từ trừu tượng phụ thuộc vào việc ý niệm đang được nói chung, là một trường hợp cụ thể hay là một khái niệm đã được xác định.

formulae: zero article + abstract noun = general concept
whenToUse: Choose zero, a/an or the according to how specifically the abstract idea is framed in the discourse.

positive: Freedom requires responsibility.
The freedom we gained after the reform came with new responsibilities.
A deep understanding of context is essential for accurate interpretation.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Articles with modifiers and unique reference
records.objective: Use article choice when restrictive modifiers make reference identifiable.

concept.en: A restrictive modifier can make a noun identifiable, while a non-specific modified noun may still require a/an.
concept.vi: Bổ ngữ hạn định có thể khiến danh từ trở nên xác định, trong khi một danh từ có bổ ngữ nhưng vẫn chưa xác định có thể tiếp tục dùng a/an.

whenToUse: Use article choice together with relative clauses and other modifiers to signal whether the listener can identify the referent.

positive: The information in the appendix is confidential.
A solution that satisfies both teams will be difficult to find.
The engineer who designed the system will join us later.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Generic reference with a/an, the and zero article
records.objective: Choose among three generic patterns based on noun type and style.

concept.en: English can express a whole class with a zero-article plural, with the + singular for a species/class, or with a/an + singular for a representative member.
concept.vi: Tiếng Anh có thể nói về cả một lớp bằng danh từ số nhiều không mạo từ, the + số ít để chỉ loài/lớp, hoặc a/an + số ít để lấy một thành viên làm đại diện.

whenToUse: Choose a generic pattern according to noun type, register and whether the class or a representative member is foregrounded.

positive: Tigers are powerful predators.
The tiger is threatened by habitat loss.
A smartphone can replace several everyday devices.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Less/fewer, number/amount and quantity precision
records.objective: Match quantifiers and measure nouns to countability.

concept.en: Fewer and number normally combine with countable plural nouns, while less and amount normally combine with uncountable quantity.
concept.vi: Fewer và number thường đi với danh từ đếm được số nhiều, còn less và amount thường đi với lượng không đếm được.

whenToUse: Make quantity language precise in formal and neutral contexts by matching the expression to countability.

positive: Fewer employees commute every day than they did five years ago.
The amount of waste produced by the factory has fallen significantly.
We need less time but a greater number of volunteers.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: A great deal of, hardly any, a large number/amount of
records.objective: Use formal and nuanced quantity expressions.

concept.en: Advanced quantifiers distinguish countability, degree and register, including a great deal of, hardly any and a large number or amount of.
concept.vi: Các lượng từ nâng cao phân biệt tính đếm được, mức độ và sắc thái văn phong, chẳng hạn a great deal of, hardly any và a large number/amount of.

formulae: a great deal of + uncountable noun
a large number of + plural noun
a large amount of + uncountable noun
whenToUse: Use nuanced quantity expressions when simple much/many is too weak or too informal for the context.

positive: A great deal of research has focused on this question.
Hardly any applicants had experience with the new platform.
A large number of residents opposed the proposal.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: The more..., the more...
records.objective: Express linked changes with correlative comparatives.

concept.en: The correlative pattern the + comparative ..., the + comparative ... links two changing variables.
concept.vi: Cấu trúc tương liên the + so sánh hơn ..., the + so sánh hơn ... liên kết hai đại lượng thay đổi cùng nhau.

formulae: The + comparative + clause, the + comparative + clause
whenToUse: Express that a change in one condition is systematically associated with a change in another.

positive: The more carefully you plan, the fewer problems you are likely to face.
The longer the meeting continued, the less productive it became.
The more we automate routine tasks, the more time we can spend on analysis.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Superlative + present perfect experience
records.objective: Use patterns such as the best ... I've ever ... naturally.

concept.en: A superlative followed by a Present Perfect relative clause evaluates an experience across the speaker's life or another unfinished period.
concept.vi: Dạng so sánh nhất đi với mệnh đề Present Perfect dùng để đánh giá một trải nghiệm trong suốt cuộc đời người nói hoặc một khoảng thời gian chưa kết thúc.

formulae: the + superlative + noun + subject + have/has ever + past participle
whenToUse: Describe an extreme experience while keeping the comparison period connected to the present.

positive: This is the most demanding project I've ever managed.
It's the best documentary we've seen this year.
That was the most convincing explanation she has given so far.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Adjective order
records.objective: Order opinion, size, age, shape, color, origin, material and purpose adjectives naturally.

concept.en: When several adjectives occur before a noun, English strongly prefers a conventional semantic order rather than an arbitrary sequence.
concept.vi: Khi nhiều tính từ cùng đứng trước danh từ, tiếng Anh ưu tiên một trật tự ngữ nghĩa quen thuộc thay vì sắp xếp tùy ý.

formulae: opinion + size + age + shape + color + origin + material + purpose + noun
whenToUse: Order stacked adjectives naturally, especially in detailed descriptions and product or object descriptions.

positive: She bought a beautiful small Italian leather bag.
They restored an impressive old stone bridge.
He drives a sleek new electric sports car.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Gradable vs non-gradable adjectives and intensifiers
records.objective: Choose very, absolutely, completely, highly, deeply and similar modifiers naturally.

concept.en: Gradable adjectives combine with degree modifiers such as very or extremely, while non-gradable extremes often prefer absolutely, completely or similar intensifiers.
concept.vi: Tính từ có thang độ kết hợp với very, extremely..., còn tính từ cực trị/không có thang độ thường hợp với absolutely, completely... hơn.

whenToUse: Choose an intensifier that matches both the adjective's scale and its common collocational behavior.

positive: The instructions are absolutely essential for safe operation.
I was deeply disappointed by the decision.
The final stage is extremely difficult but not impossible.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Stance adverbs
records.objective: Use apparently, obviously, fortunately, arguably and similar items to mark speaker stance.

concept.en: Stance adverbs comment on the speaker's certainty, evaluation or attitude toward the whole proposition.
concept.vi: Trạng từ lập trường cho biết mức độ chắc chắn, đánh giá hoặc thái độ của người nói đối với toàn bộ mệnh đề.

whenToUse: Signal evidence, evaluation or viewpoint explicitly without changing the core event described.

positive: Apparently, the supplier has changed its delivery schedule.
Fortunately, nobody was injured in the accident.
Arguably, this is the most important finding in the report.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Focus adverbs: even, only, just, also
records.objective: Place focus adverbs to control what part of a sentence is emphasized.

concept.en: Focus adverbs such as only, even, just and also change which constituent receives emphasis, so their position can change meaning.
concept.vi: Các trạng từ tiêu điểm như only, even, just và also thay đổi thành phần được nhấn mạnh, vì vậy vị trí của chúng có thể làm đổi nghĩa.

formulae: focus adverb immediately before the focused constituent where possible
whenToUse: Place focus adverbs deliberately to distinguish who, what action or which object is being restricted or highlighted.

positive: Only Maya reviewed the final draft.
Maya only reviewed the final draft, so she did not approve it.
Even the most experienced engineers found the task difficult.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Fixed prepositional phrases
records.objective: Use common multiword patterns such as in charge of, on behalf of and in response to.

concept.en: Many formal and neutral meanings are expressed through fixed multiword prepositional phrases whose internal preposition is not freely interchangeable.
concept.vi: Nhiều ý nghĩa trung tính và trang trọng được diễn đạt bằng cụm giới từ cố định nhiều từ, trong đó giới từ bên trong không thể thay tùy ý.

whenToUse: Use established phrase-level combinations for roles, responses, reference and formal connections between ideas.

positive: On behalf of the team, I'd like to thank everyone who helped.
She is in charge of coordinating the regional offices.
The policy was revised in response to customer feedback.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Advanced adjective + preposition patterns
records.objective: Master less predictable adjective complement choices and meaning changes.

concept.en: Many adjectives select a particular preposition, and changing that preposition can be ungrammatical or alter the intended relation.
concept.vi: Nhiều tính từ đòi hỏi một giới từ cụ thể; đổi giới từ có thể làm câu sai hoặc thay đổi quan hệ nghĩa.

whenToUse: Learn adjective-preposition combinations as lexical patterns rather than translating the preposition literally.

positive: The committee is aware of the risks involved.
This approach is consistent with our long-term strategy.
She is capable of handling the negotiation herself.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Advanced verb + preposition patterns
records.objective: Master verb-preposition combinations whose meaning depends on the preposition.

concept.en: Many verbs form meaning-specific patterns with a required preposition that should be learned together with the verb.
concept.vi: Nhiều động từ tạo thành mẫu nghĩa cụ thể với một giới từ bắt buộc và nên được học như một đơn vị cùng với động từ.

whenToUse: Choose the preposition licensed by the verb and intended meaning instead of translating a Vietnamese preposition word-for-word.

positive: We need to distinguish between temporary failures and structural problems.
The success of the campaign depends on sustained public support.
Several experts objected to the proposed change.

provenance.note: Project-original controlled B2 grammar-body content; publication is review-ledger only.

records.title: Phrasal-prepositional and multiword verbs
records.objective: Distinguish particle, preposition and three-word verb patterns.

concept.en: Multiword verbs combine a lexical verb with particles and/or prepositions; the whole combination controls meaning, object position and complement pattern.
